title.zh: 卷三百二十四 列傳第八十三 石普 張孜 許懷德 李允則 張亢 劉文質 趙滋
title.en: Volume 324 Biographies 83: Shi Pu, Zhang Zi, Xu Huaide, Li Yunze, Zhang Kang, Liu Wenzhi, Zhao Zi
title.raw: 卷三百二十四 列傳第八十三 石普 張孜 許懷德 李允則 張亢 劉文質 趙滋 Volume 324 Biographies 83: Shi Pu, Zhang Zi, Xu Huaide, Li Yunze, Zhang Kang, Liu Wenzhi, Zhao Zi

sentences.zh: 石普，其先幽州人，自言唐河中節度雄之後，徙居太原。

translations.literal: Shi Pu — his ancestors were men of Youzhou; he himself said he was a descendant of Xiong, Military Governor of Hezhong under the Tang, and moved his household to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu came from Youzhou stock; he claimed descent from Xiong, the Tang military governor of Hezhong, and his family later settled in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖全，事周為鐵騎軍使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Quan served the Zhou as commissioner of the Iron Cavalry Army.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Quan had served the Later Zhou as commander of the Iron Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 父通，事太宗於晉邸。

translations.literal: His father Tong served Taizong at the Prince of Jin's residence.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tong had attended the future Emperor Taizong when he was still prince at the Jin residence.

sentences.zh: 普十歲給事邸中，以謹信見親，補寄班祗候，再遷東頭供奉官。

translations.literal: At age ten Pu was assigned to serve in the residence; because of his prudence and trustworthiness he was regarded with intimacy, was appointed Acting Class Attendant-on-Duty, and was promoted twice to Eastern Head Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Pu entered princely service at ten. His steadiness won him favor; he was made an acting attendant on the heir's staff and twice promoted to eastern head palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 賊邢橐駝、賈禿指數百人寇掠永興諸縣，命普督兵往捕，悉獲之。

translations.literal: The bandits Xing Tuoluo and Jia Tuzhi with several hundred men raided and plundered the counties of Yongxing; [the court] ordered Pu to supervise troops to go and capture them, and all were seized.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits led by Xing Tuoluo and Jia Tuzhi, several hundred strong, were raiding Yongxing's counties. Pu was ordered to lead troops against them and took every one.

sentences.zh: 遷內殿崇班、帶御器械。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inner Hall Esteemed Class and Bearer of the Imperial Arms.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to inner hall honored guard and imperial arms bearer.

sentences.zh: 李順叛，普為西川行營先鋒，與韓守英、馬知節誅斬之。

translations.literal: When Li Shun rebelled, Pu was vanguard of the Western Sichuan Field Army; together with Han Shouying and Ma Zhijie he executed and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shun rose in rebellion, Pu served as vanguard of the western Sichuan campaign force and, with Han Shouying and Ma Zhijie, killed him.

sentences.zh: 遷西京作坊使、欽州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Western Capital Workshop Commissioner and Prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commissioner of the western capital workshops and prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 順餘黨復寇邛蜀，偽稱邛南王。

translations.literal: Li Shun's remaining partisans again raided Qiong and Shu, falsely styling themselves King of Southern Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shun's remaining followers raided Qiong and Shu again and proclaimed a King of Southern Qiong.

sentences.zh: 又為西川都提舉捉賊使。

translations.literal: He again was made Overall Suppressing-Bandits Commissioner for Western Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed overall bandit-suppression commissioner for western Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 時蜀民疑不自安，多欲為盜者，普因馳入對，面陳：「蜀亂由賦斂苛急，農民失業，宜稍蠲減之，使自為生，則不討而自平矣。」

translations.literal: At that time the people of Shu, doubting and ill at ease, many wished to become bandits; Pu therefore galloped in to an audience and in person stated: "The turmoil in Shu comes from harsh and urgent tax levies; the farmers have lost their livelihoods. It is fitting to reduce them somewhat and let them make their own living — then without campaigning they will pacify themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan's people were uneasy and mistrustful; many were ready to turn bandit. Pu rode posthaste to court and argued in person: "The unrest in Shu springs from crushing taxes. Farmers have lost their livelihood. Lighten the levies a little and let people support themselves again, and the province will settle without another expedition."

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 普即日還蜀，揭榜諭之，莫不悅服。

translations.literal: Pu that same day returned to Shu, posted placards to instruct them, and none were not pleased and submissive.
translations.idiomatic: Pu returned to Sichuan the same day, posted notices explaining the change, and won the people's willing obedience.

sentences.zh: 賊平，賜白金三千兩、襲衣、金帶、鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, he was bestowed three thousand taels of white gold, a robe of investiture, a gold belt, and a saddled and bridled horse.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed, he received three thousand taels of silver, ceremonial robes, a gold belt, and a saddled horse from the throne.

sentences.zh: 累遷洛苑使、富州團練使、延州緣邊都巡檢使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Luoyuan Commissioner, Fuzhou Militia Training Commissioner, and Yanzhou Frontier Comprehensive Patrol Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through appointments as Luoyuan commissioner, Fuzhou militia training commissioner, and comprehensive frontier patrol commissioner at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 羌酋乜羽內寇，普追殺之。

translations.literal: The Qiang chieftain Miye invaded inward; Pu pursued and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiang leader Miye raided inward, Pu pursued and killed him.

sentences.zh: 從真宗幸大名，會王均叛，以為川峽路招安巡檢使，佐雷有終率諸將進討。

translations.literal: He followed Zhenzong on a visit to Daming; it happened that Wang Jun rebelled — he was made Sichuan Gorge Route Pacification and Patrol Commissioner to assist Lei Youzhong in leading the various generals forward to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying Emperor Zhenzong to Daming, he was caught up in Wang Jun's rebellion. He was named pacification and patrol commissioner for the Sichuan gorges route to assist Lei Youzhong in leading the generals against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 至天回鎮，賊出拒戰，普領前陣力擊破之。

translations.literal: When they reached Tianhui Town, the bandits came out to resist in battle; Pu led the forward array and with force struck and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianhui town the rebels came out to fight. Pu led the van and broke them in a fierce assault.

sentences.zh: 賊退保益州，王師圍城數月不下，普繕車炮，又為地道攻城。

translations.literal: The bandits retreated to hold Yizhou; the imperial army besieged the city several months without taking it — Pu repaired siege carts and artillery and moreover made an underground tunnel to assault the city.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back on Yizhou. Imperial troops besieged the city for months without success. Pu repaired siege engines and catapults and opened a tunnel assault.

sentences.zh: 城破，均夜半突圍，由南門遁，普引兵追擊於富順監，均自殺，餘黨皆平。

translations.literal: When the city was broken, Jun at midnight broke out of the encirclement and fled through the south gate; Pu led troops in pursuit and struck at Fushun Jian; Jun killed himself, and the remaining partisans were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Wang Jun broke out at midnight through the south gate. Pu pursued him to Fushun and forced him to kill himself; the remaining rebels were pacified.

sentences.zh: 遷冀州團練使，賜黃金三百兩、白金三千兩。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jizhou Militia Training Commissioner and bestowed three hundred taels of yellow gold and three thousand taels of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to militia training commissioner of Jizhou and rewarded with three hundred taels of gold and three thousand of silver.

sentences.zh: 故事，正任不兼帶御器械，帝特以命普。

translations.literal: By precedent, those in regular appointment did not concurrently bear the Imperial Arms; the Emperor specially so ordered Pu.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, regular provincial appointees did not also carry the imperial arms privilege; the emperor made an exception for Pu.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯邊，為保州兵馬鈐轄、北面行營押策先鋒，與契丹戰廉良城，又戰長城口，獲俘馘器甲甚眾。

translations.literal: When the Khitan violated the border, he was made Baozhou Military Horse and Militia Supervisor and vanguard of the Northern Field Army strategic-planning staff; he battled the Khitan at Liangliang City and again at Changcheng Pass, capturing prisoners, severed heads, weapons, and armor in very great number.
translations.idiomatic: During a Khitan border raid he served as Baozhou military supervisor and strategic-planning vanguard on the northern field staff. He fought them at Liangliang city and again at Changcheng pass, taking many prisoners and a large haul of weapons and armor.

sentences.zh: 徙定州路副都總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Deputy Overall Commander of Dingzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as deputy overall commander on the Dingzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 靈州失守，益兵備關中，徙永興軍副都總管。

translations.literal: When Lingzhou was lost, troops were increased to defend Guanzhong; he was transferred to Yongxing Army Deputy Overall Commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Lingzhou fell, reinforcements were sent to secure Guanzhong, and Pu became deputy overall commander of the Yongxing army.

sentences.zh: 時軍製疏略，凡號令進退，及呼召將佐、會合別屯，皆遣人馳告。

translations.literal: At that time military regulations were coarse and brief: whenever orders to advance or retire, and summoning officers or joining separate encampments, all were done by sending men on galloping report.
translations.idiomatic: Military procedures were still crude: orders to advance, retreat, summon officers, or unite separate camps all went out by mounted messenger.

sentences.zh: 普上請曰：「臣嘗將兵，輒破一錢，與別將各持半，用相合為信。」

translations.literal: Pu submitted a request, saying: "Your servant once commanded troops and would break a coin in two, each general holding half, using their joining as proof of trust."
translations.idiomatic: Pu petitioned the throne: "When I commanded troops, I would break a coin in half—each commander kept one piece, and matching halves proved the message was genuine."

sentences.zh: 帝為置傳信牌，漆木長六寸，闊三寸，腹背刻字而中分之，置鑿枘令可合。

translations.literal: The Emperor therefore had communication tokens made — lacquered wood six inches long and three inches wide, characters carved on belly and back and then split down the middle, with mortise and tenon made so they could join.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered communication tokens made: lacquered wooden plaques six inches long and three wide, inscribed on both sides and split in half with a mortise-and-tenon joint so the pieces would fit together.

sentences.zh: 又穿二竅，容筆墨，上施紙劄，每臨陣則分持，或傳令則書其言，繫軍吏之頸，至彼為合契。

translations.literal: Moreover two holes were bored to hold brush and ink; paper slips were attached on top. Each time they took the field they divided and held them; or when transmitting orders they wrote the words, tied them to a military clerk's neck, and at the destination joined them as matching tokens.
translations.idiomatic: Each token had two holes for brush and ink and a paper slip attached. Before battle the halves were distributed; orders could be written on the slip, tied to a courier's neck, and matched at the other camp to verify authenticity.

sentences.zh: 又獻《禦戎圖》，請設塹以陷敵馬，並上所置戰械甚眾。

translations.literal: He also presented the Diagram for Controlling the Barbarians, requesting ditches be set to trap enemy horses, and together submitted the many war engines he had devised.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted his Defenses against the Barbarians, proposing ditches to trap enemy horses, along with numerous siege devices of his own design.

sentences.zh: 徙為莫州總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Overall Commander of Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as overall commander of Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 初，契丹南侵，敗我兵於望都。

translations.literal: At first, when the Khitan invaded south, they defeated our army at Wangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Khitan raided south, they had routed Song forces at Wangdu.

sentences.zh: 既而諜者言復欲大入寇，帝自畫軍事，以手詔示輔臣曰：

translations.literal: Before long spies reported they wished again to invade on a large scale; the Emperor himself drew up the military plan and, with a handwritten edict, showed the chief ministers, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Soon intelligence reported another major invasion. The emperor drafted the campaign plan himself and showed his chief ministers a handwritten edict:

sentences.zh: 鎮、定、高陽三路兵宜會定州，夾唐河為大陣，立柵以守。

translations.literal: The armies of the three routes Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang should assemble at Dingzhou, with the Tang River between them forming the great formation, erecting palisades to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Forces from the Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang circuits should concentrate at Dingzhou, straddling the Tang River in a fortified main camp.

sentences.zh: 量寇遠近出軍。

translations.literal: According to the enemy's distance, send out troops.
translations.idiomatic: Deploy detachments according to how far the enemy had advanced.

sentences.zh: 俟敵疲則先鋒出致師，用騎卒居中，環以步卒，接短兵而已，無遠離隊伍。

translations.literal: Wait until the enemy is weary, then let the vanguard go out to offer battle; use cavalry in the center, ringed with infantry — engage only at close quarters, and do not stray far from the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy tired, the vanguard would offer battle: cavalry in the center, infantry around them, fighting only at close range and never leaving the formation.

sentences.zh: 又分兵出三路：以六千騎屯威虜軍，魏能、白守素、張銳領之；

translations.literal: Moreover divide the army into three routes: six thousand cavalry stationed at Weilu Army, led by Wei Neng, Bai Shousu, and Zhang Rui;
translations.idiomatic: Three detached cavalry commands were also set: six thousand horsemen at Weilu, under Wei Neng, Bai Shousu, and Zhang Rui;

sentences.zh: 五千騎屯保州，楊延昭、張禧、李懷岊領之；

translations.literal: five thousand cavalry stationed at Baozhou, led by Yang Yanzhao, Zhang Xi, and Li Huaizhe;
translations.idiomatic: five thousand at Baozhou, under Yang Yanzhao, Zhang Xi, and Li Huaizhe;

sentences.zh: 五千騎屯北平塞，田敏、楊凝、石延福領之，以當賊鋒。

translations.literal: five thousand cavalry stationed at Beiping Fort, led by Tian Min, Yang Ning, and Shi Yanfu, to meet the enemy's spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: and five thousand at Beiping pass, under Tian Min, Yang Ning, and Shi Yanfu, to blunt the enemy's advance.

sentences.zh: 始至勿輕鬥，待其氣衰，背城以戰。

translations.literal: At first arrival do not fight lightly; wait until their spirit declines, then with the city at your back give battle.
translations.idiomatic: They were not to engage rashly on arrival, but to wait until Khitan morale flagged and then fight with the city at their backs.

sentences.zh: 若南越保州，與大軍遇，則令威虜之師與延昭會，使腹背受敵。

translations.literal: If they passed south of Baozhou and met the great army, then order the Weilu force to join with Yanzhao, making the enemy attacked from belly and back.
translations.idiomatic: If the Khitan slipped south of Baozhou and ran into the main army, the Weilu and Baozhou commands would unite so the enemy would be caught between two forces.

sentences.zh: 若不攻定州，縱軼南侵，則復會北平田敏，合勢入契丹界，邀其輜重，令雄、霸、破虜已來，互為聲援。

translations.literal: If they did not attack Dingzhou but let their horses run south in raid, then again join Beiping's Tian Min, combine strength to enter Khitan territory, intercept their baggage train, and from Xiong, Ba, and Pohuo onward mutually support one another.
translations.idiomatic: If they bypassed Dingzhou and raided deeper south, Tian Min at Beiping would combine with them, strike into Liao territory to cut off supply trains, and coordinate with garrisons from Xiongzhou, Bazhou, and Pohuo southward.

sentences.zh: 又命孫全照、五德鈞、裴自榮將兵八千屯寧邊軍，李重貴、趙守倫、張繼旻將兵五千屯邢州，扼東西路。

translations.literal: Moreover he ordered Sun Quanzhao, Wu Dejun, and Pei Zirong to lead eight thousand troops stationed at Ningbian Army; Li Chonggui, Zhao Shoulun, and Zhang Jimin to lead five thousand stationed at Xingzhou, blocking the eastern and western roads.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quanzhao, Wu Dejun, and Pei Zirong were to hold Ningbian with eight thousand men; Li Chonggui, Zhao Shoulun, and Zhang Jimin would block the eastern and western approaches from Xingzhou with five thousand.

sentences.zh: 契丹將遁，則令定州大軍與三路騎兵會擊之，令普統軍一萬於莫州，盧文壽、王守俊監之，敵騎北去，則西趨順安軍襲擊，斷西山之路。

translations.literal: When the Khitan were about to flee, then order the Dingzhou great army and the three-route cavalry to join in striking them; order Pu to command ten thousand troops at Mozhou, supervised by Lu Wenshou and Wang Shoujun — when enemy cavalry went north, then hurry west toward Shun'an Army to strike, cutting the western mountain road.
translations.idiomatic: If the Khitan withdrew, the Dingzhou main force and the three cavalry commands would converge on them. Pu would command ten thousand men at Mozhou under Lu Wenshou and Wang Shoujun; if enemy horsemen fled north, he was to strike west toward Shun'an and sever their escape through the western hills.

sentences.zh: 如河冰已合，敵由東路，則劉用、劉漢凝、田思明以兵五千會普、全照為掎角，仍命石保吉將萬兵鎮大名，以張軍勢。

translations.literal: If the river ice had already joined and the enemy came by the eastern road, then Liu Yong, Liu Hanning, and Tian Siming with five thousand troops would join Pu and Quanzhao in pincer action; moreover he ordered Shi Baoji to lead ten thousand troops to secure Daming, to display military might.
translations.idiomatic: If the rivers froze and the enemy used the eastern route, Liu Yong, Liu Hanning, and Tian Siming would bring five thousand men to support Pu and Quanzhao in a pincer. Shi Baoji would hold Daming with ten thousand to magnify the army's presence.

sentences.zh: 繢圖以授諸將。

translations.literal: He painted a diagram and gave it to the various generals.
translations.idiomatic: He had the plan painted as a chart and issued it to his commanders.

sentences.zh: 後數月，敕輔臣曰：「北邊已屯大兵，而邊奏至，敵未有釁，且聚軍虛費，民力何以給之？

translations.literal: Several months later he charged the chief ministers: "The northern border has already massed great armies, yet border reports arrive and the enemy shows no sign of trouble — yet gathering troops wastes resources in vain; how can the people's strength supply it?
translations.idiomatic: Months later he instructed his ministers: "We have massed huge forces on the northern frontier, yet the border reports no enemy movement. Keeping this army idle wastes the people's strength—how long can we sustain it?

sentences.zh: 宜有制畫，以為控遏。

translations.literal: There should be a regulated plan to serve as control and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: We need a measured plan to hold the frontier without ruinous expense.

sentences.zh: 且靜戎、順安軍界，先開營田、河道，可以扼黑盧口、三台、小李路，亦可通漕運至邊。

translations.literal: Moreover, on the border of Jingrong and Shun'an armies, first open military colonies and waterways — they can choke Heilukou, Santai, and Xiaoli roads, and can also connect grain transport by canal to the border.
translations.idiomatic: Between Jingrong and Shun'an we should open military farms and canals to block Heilukou, Santai, and the Xiaoli route and extend the grain supply line to the border.

sentences.zh: 宜乘此用眾浚治，使及軍城，彼或撓吾役，即合兵擊之。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to take advantage of this and use troops to dredge and repair, so that it reaches the military cities; if they should disrupt our work, then combine forces and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Use the army now to dig canals and extend them to the frontier garrisons; if the Khitan interfere, unite and drive them off.

sentences.zh: 李沆等曰：「設險以製敵，守邊之利也。」

translations.literal: Li Hang and others said: "Setting barriers to restrain the enemy is the profit of defending the border."
translations.idiomatic: Li Hang and others replied: "Fortifying the frontier to contain the enemy is the soundest border policy."

sentences.zh: 遂詔內侍閻文慶與靜戎、順安知軍事王能、馬濟督其事，而徙普屯順安之西，與威虜魏能、保州楊延昭、北平田敏為掎角。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the inner attendant Yan Wenqing together with Jingrong and Shun'an military affairs commissioners Wang Neng and Ma Ji to supervise the matter, while transferring Pu to camp west of Shun'an, with Weilu's Wei Neng, Baozhou's Yang Yanzhao, and Beiping's Tian Min in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the eunuch Yan Wenqing with Wang Neng and Ma Ji, who commanded Jingrong and Shun'an, to oversee the works, and moved Pu west of Shun'an to coordinate with Wei Neng, Yang Yanzhao, and Tian Min in a mutual-support triangle.

sentences.zh: 內侍馮仁俊掌御劍於莫州，與普不叶。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Feng Renjun held the Imperial Sword at Mozhou and did not harmonize with Pu.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Feng Renjun, who carried the imperial sword at Mozhou, clashed with Pu.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「勿窮治以驕將帥。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Do not pursue the matter to the end lest the generals grow arrogant."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Do not press the investigation too far and spoil our commanders' morale."

sentences.zh: 第召仁俊還。

translations.literal: He only summoned Renjun back.
translations.idiomatic: He simply recalled Renjun to court.

sentences.zh: 又令普率所部屯乾寧軍，復遷普冀州團練使，徙本州總管。

translations.literal: He again ordered Pu to lead his command to camp at Qianning Army; he again transferred Pu to Jizhou Militia Training Commissioner and moved him to overall commander of his home prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was ordered to move his troops to Qianning; he was again made militia training commissioner of Jizhou and overall commander of his home circuit.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸澶淵，時王繼忠已陷契丹，契丹欲請和，因繼忠遣人持信箭為書遺普，且通密表。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Chanyuan, at that time Wang Jizhong had already surrendered to the Khitan; the Khitan wished to request peace and, through Jizhong, sent a man bearing a trust arrow as a letter to Pu, and also sent a secret memorial.
translations.idiomatic: During the emperor's stay at Chanyuan, Wang Jizhong had already gone over to the Khitan, who now sought peace. Through Jizhong they sent a messenger with a trust arrow and a secret message to Pu.

sentences.zh: 事平，遷容州觀察使。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was transferred to Observer of Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was concluded, he was promoted to military commissioner of Rongzhou.

sentences.zh: 向敏中為鄜延路都總管，以普副之。

translations.literal: Xiang Minzhong was Overall Commander of the Fuyan Route; Pu was made his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Minzhong became overall commander on the Fuyan circuit, Pu served as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 趙德明納款，詔降制命，普言：「不宜授以押蕃落使，使之總制屬羌，則強橫不可制矣。」

translations.literal: When Zhao Deming submitted allegiance, an edict was about to lower a formal appointment; Pu said: "It is not fitting to grant him the post of Overseer of Fan Tribes, making him overall control the subordinate Qiang — then he will be overbearing and cannot be restrained."
translations.idiomatic: As Zhao Deming came in to submit, the court prepared a formal commission. Pu warned: "Do not make him overseer of the frontier tribes and give him authority over all the Qiang—once strengthened, he will be impossible to control."

sentences.zh: 乃止兼管內蕃落使。

translations.literal: Thereupon they stopped his concurrent charge as Inner Overseer of Fan Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The court therefore dropped the concurrent post of inner overseer of frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徙幷代路，給公使錢二千五百緡，普援例歲給錢三千緡，樞密院言無此例。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to the Bingdai Route and given two thousand five hundred strings of public envoy money; Pu cited precedent for three thousand strings yearly — the Bureau of Military Affairs said there was no such precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was posted to the Bingdai circuit with 2,500 strings of envoy funds; Pu cited precedent for 3,000 strings a year, but the Bureau of Military Affairs denied the claim.

sentences.zh: 又言李漢超守河朔時，歲給以萬計，今幷代屯軍多，不足以犒軍，帝不納。

translations.literal: He also said that when Li Hanchao held the Hebei north, yearly grants ran to tens of thousands — now Bingdai's stationed troops were many and insufficient to reward the army; the Emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that Li Hanchao on the Hebei frontier had once received annual payments in the tens of thousands, whereas Bingdai's larger garrison could not be sustained on the present allowance. The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 改桂州觀察使、鎮州路總管，遷保平軍節度觀察留後，赴本鎮。

translations.literal: He was changed to Observer of Guizhou and Overall Commander of Zhenzhou Circuit, transferred to Military Commissioner and Observation Remnant of Baoping Army, and proceeded to his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as observer of Guizhou and overall commander on the Zhenzhou circuit, then as acting military commissioner of Baoping, and went to take up his post.

sentences.zh: 帝祀汾陰，還至陝西，普請駐蹕城中。

translations.literal: When the Emperor performed sacrifice at Fenyin, on the return he reached Shaanxi; Pu requested that the imperial halt be within the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from the Fenyin sacrifices, the emperor reached Shaanxi; Pu urged him to lodge inside the city walls.

sentences.zh: 因賜詩，令扈從至西京。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was bestowed a poem and ordered to escort him as far as the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded him with a poem and had him escort the procession to the western capital.

sentences.zh: 拜河西軍節度使、知河陽，徙許州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Commissioner of Hexi Army and Administrator of Heyang, then transferred to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military commissioner of Hexi and administrator of Heyang, then transferred to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 築大流堰，引河通漕京師。

translations.literal: He built the Great Flowing Weir, drawing the river to connect grain transport by canal to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He constructed the Great Flowing Weir, diverting the Yellow River to feed the capital's grain transport canals.

sentences.zh: 上《軍儀條目》二卷、《用將機宜要訣》二圖。

translations.literal: He submitted two scrolls of Military Regulations Articles and two diagrams of Essentials for Employing Generals.
translations.idiomatic: He presented two scrolls of military regulations and two illustrated manuals on the use of generals.

sentences.zh: 時方崇尚符瑞，而普請罷天下醮設，歲可省緡錢七十餘萬，以贍國用，繇是忤帝意。

translations.literal: At that time they were just then honoring auspicious portents, yet Pu requested abolishing Daoist prayer assemblies throughout the realm — yearly more than seven hundred thousand strings could be saved to supply state expenditure — and thereby offended the Emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: The court was promoting miraculous signs, but Pu urged an end to empire-wide Daoist prayer assemblies, arguing the savings—over seven hundred thousand strings a year—should go to state expenses. The emperor took offense.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符九年，上言九月下旬日食者三；

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, he submitted a memorial that in the last ten days of the ninth month there would be three solar eclipses;
translations.idiomatic: In 1016, he memorialized that three solar eclipses would occur in the last ten days of the ninth month;

sentences.zh: 又言：「商賈自秦州來，言唃廝囉欲陰報曹瑋，請以臣所獻陣圖付瑋，可使瑋必勝。」

translations.literal: he also said: "Merchants coming from Qinzhou report that Gusiluo wishes secretly to strike Cao Wei — I request that the battle array diagrams your servant presented be given to Wei, and Wei can be made certain to win."
translations.idiomatic: and added: "Traders from Qinzhou say Gusiluo plans a secret attack on Cao Wei. Give him the battle diagrams I submitted, and Wei will surely prevail."

sentences.zh: 帝以普言逾分，而樞密使王欽若言普欲以邊事動朝廷，帝怒，命知雜御史呂夷簡劾之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Pu's words exceeded his station, and because Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Qinruo said Pu wished to stir the court with border affairs, was angry and ordered the miscellaneous censor Lü Yijian to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged Pu's speech presumptuous; Wang Qinruo of the Bureau of Military Affairs said Pu was trying to alarm the court with frontier crises. Enraged, the emperor ordered Lü Yijian to investigate.

sentences.zh: 獄具，集百官參驗，九月下旬日不食。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, he assembled the hundred officials to examine together — in the last ten days of the ninth month the sun did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: When the case closed, the court assembled officials to verify his claims: no eclipse had occurred in late ninth month.

sentences.zh: 坐普私藏天文，下百官雜議，罪當死。

translations.literal: Pu was convicted of privately hoarding astronomical [works]; the hundred officials deliberated together — the crime warranted death.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was found guilty of privately possessing astronomical texts. The assembled officials ruled the offense capital.

sentences.zh: 議以官當。

translations.literal: In deliberation they used office to offset punishment.
translations.idiomatic: They commuted the death sentence by rank.

sentences.zh: 詔除名，貶賀州，遣使縶送流所。

translations.literal: An edict removed his name [from office], demoted him to Hezhou, and sent an envoy to bind and escort him to his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of office, demoted to Hezhou, and bound under escort to his place of exile.

sentences.zh: 帝謂輔臣曰：「普出微賤，性輕躁，干求不已。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to the chief ministers: "Pu came from the very lowly; his nature is light and rash, and he seeks favors without end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers: "Pu rose from nothing. He is impulsive and never stops angling for favor.

sentences.zh: 既懵文藝，而假手撰述，以揣摩時事。

translations.literal: He is ignorant of literary arts, yet borrows another's hand to compose and write, to fathom and stroke the times.
translations.idiomatic: He has no learning, yet hires ghostwriters to sound learned and court the mood of the moment.

sentences.zh: 聞在繫所，思其幼子，時時泣下，可聽挈家以行。」

translations.literal: Hearing that in prison he thinks of his young son and from time to time weeps — he may be permitted to bring his family when he goes."
translations.idiomatic: They say he weeps in prison for his young son. Let him take his family into exile."

sentences.zh: 甫至賀州，授太子左清道率府副率、房州安置，增房州屯兵百人護守。

translations.literal: When he had just reached Hezhou, he was appointed Vice Commandant of the Left Qingdao Rate of the Heir Apparent's Household, with residence assigned at Fangzhou, and a hundred Fangzhou garrison troops added to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he reached Hezhou when he was given a nominal post in the heir apparent's household and confined at Fangzhou with a hundred extra guards.

sentences.zh: 普倜儻有膽略，凡預討伐，聞敵所在，即馳赴之。

translations.literal: Pu was unrestrained and had daring and stratagem; whenever he took part in campaigns, hearing where the enemy was, he would gallop to go there.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was bold and resourceful; in every campaign, as soon as he learned where the enemy was, he rode straight for them.

sentences.zh: 兩平蜀盜，大小數十戰，摧鋒與賊角，眾推其勇。

translations.literal: He twice pacified Shu bandits, in large and small several tens of battles, crushed the spearhead and grappled with the enemy — the masses praised his courage.
translations.idiomatic: He helped suppress two Sichuan rebellions in dozens of fights, always leading the charge; soldiers acclaimed his bravery.

sentences.zh: 頗通兵書、陰陽、六甲、星曆、推步之術。

translations.literal: He was quite versed in military books, yin and yang, the six jia, stars and calendars, and calculation by steps.
translations.idiomatic: He was well read in military classics, divination, calendrics, and astrology.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗曰：「普性剛驁，與諸將少合。」

translations.literal: Taizong once said: "Pu's nature is stern and proud; with the various generals he seldom harmonizes."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once remarked: "Pu is stiff-necked and rarely gets on with other commanders."

sentences.zh: 然藉其善戰，每厚遇之。

translations.literal: Yet relying on his skill in battle, each time he treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Still, valuing his fighting ability, he always treated him well.

sentences.zh: 後以罪廢，每太宗忌日，必盡室詣佛寺齋薦，率以為常。

translations.literal: Later, because of his crime he was dismissed; on each anniversary of Taizong's death he would bring the whole household to Buddhist temples for fasting offerings, making it his constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: After his disgrace he observed every anniversary of Taizong's death by taking his entire household to Buddhist temples for memorial offerings—a habit he never broke.

sentences.zh: 張孜，開封人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zi was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zi was a native of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 母微時生孜，後入宮乳悼獻太子。

translations.literal: His mother, when still humble, bore Zi; later she entered the palace to nurse the deceased heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His mother bore him while she was still a commoner; later she entered the palace as wet nurse to the late heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 孜方在繈褓，真宗以付內侍張景宗曰：「此兒貌厚，汝謹視之。」

translations.literal: Zi was still in swaddling clothes; Zhenzong handed him to the inner attendant Zhang Jingzong, saying: "This child's appearance is substantial — you watch over him carefully."
translations.idiomatic: While Zhang Zi was still an infant, Zhenzong gave him to the eunuch Zhang Jingzong, saying, "This boy looks sturdy—look after him carefully."

sentences.zh: 景宗遂養以為子。

translations.literal: Jingzong thereupon raised him as his son.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong raised him as his own son.

sentences.zh: 蔭補三班奉職、給事春坊司，轉殿直。

translations.literal: By yin privilege he was appointed Third Class Palace Attendant, served in the Crown Prince's Spring Palace Office, and was transferred to Hall Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service by hereditary privilege as a third-class palace attendant in the heir apparent's household and was promoted to hall direct attendant.

sentences.zh: 契丹欲背盟，富弼往使，命孜為副，議論雖出弼，然孜亦安重習事。

translations.literal: The Khitan wished to break the treaty; Fu Bi went as envoy, and Zi was ordered as deputy — although the deliberations came from Bi, yet Zi was also steady and experienced in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan threatened to renounce the treaty, Fu Bi led the embassy and Zhang Zi served as deputy. Fu Bi shaped the policy, but Zi was steady and knew the business.

sentences.zh: 以勞遷西上閤門使、知瀛州，拜單州團練使、龍神衛四廂都指揮使、幷代副總管。

translations.literal: For his labors he was transferred to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and Administrator of Yingzhou, appointed Shanzhou Militia Training Commissioner, Dragon Divine Guard Fourth Barracks Overall Commander, and Bingdai Deputy Overall Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded for his service, he became western upper gate commissioner and prefect of Yingzhou, then militia training commissioner of Shanzhou, overall commander of the fourth dragon divine guard barracks, and deputy overall commander on the Bingdai circuit.

sentences.zh: 河東更鐵錢法，人情疑貳，兵相率扣府欲訴，閉門不納。

translations.literal: In Hedong they changed the iron cash law; popular sentiment doubted and was divided — soldiers together went to knock on the government office wishing to appeal, and [the officials] closed the gate and would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong revised its iron-cash currency, stirring public distrust. Troops marched on the yamen to protest, and officials shut the gates against them.

sentences.zh: 是日幾亂，孜策馬從數卒往諭之，皆散還營。

translations.literal: That day it nearly came to riot; Zi spurred his horse with several soldiers to go instruct them, and all dispersed back to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Riot nearly broke out that day. Zhang Zi rode out with a handful of men, talked the soldiers down, and sent them back to camp.

sentences.zh: 遷濟州防禦使、侍衛馬軍都虞候，又遷殿前都虞候，加桂州管內觀察使，遷侍衛步軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Defender of Jizhou and Chief Commandant of the Palace Horse Guards, again transferred to Chief Commandant Before the Hall, with Guizhou Circuit Observer added, and transferred to Deputy Overall Commander of the Palace Foot Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He became defender of Jizhou and chief of the palace horse guards, then chief commandant before the hall with concurrent observer of Guizhou, and finally deputy overall commander of the palace foot guards.

sentences.zh: 虎翼兵教不中程，指揮使問狀，屈強不肯對，乘夜，十餘人大噪，趣往將害人，孜禽首惡斬之然後聞。

translations.literal: The Tiger Wing troops' drill did not meet standard; the commander questioned them — they were obstinate and refused to answer; in the night more than ten men made a great clamor and hurried to go harm people — Zi seized the chief culprit and beheaded him, and only then reported.
translations.idiomatic: When Tiger Wing troops failed their drill inspection, their commander questioned them; they refused to answer. That night a dozen men raised a clamor and moved to kill their officers. Zhang Zi seized the ringleader, executed him, and only then reported the affair.

sentences.zh: 遷昭信軍節度觀察留後、馬軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Commissioner and Observation Remnant of Zhaoxin Army and Deputy Overall Commander of the Horse Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting military commissioner of Zhaoxin and deputy overall commander of the horse guards.

sentences.zh: 孜長於宮禁中，內外頗涉疑似，言者請罷孜兵柄，乃出為寧遠軍節度使、知潞州，徙陳州。

translations.literal: Zi had grown up within the palace precincts; inside and outside there was much that touched on suspicion — memorialists requested removing Zi's military authority; he was therefore sent out as Military Commissioner of Ningyuan Army and Administrator of Luzhou, then transferred to Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Having been raised inside the palace, Zhang Zi attracted suspicion on many sides. Critics urged stripping him of military power; he was sent out as military commissioner of Ningyuan and prefect of Luzhou, then moved to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁宗以其無他，復召為馬軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong, because he had no other faults, again summoned him to serve as Deputy Overall Commander of the Palace Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Finding no other fault in him, Emperor Renzong recalled him as deputy overall commander of the palace cavalry.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞韓絳又言：「孜不當典兵，而宰相富弼薦引之，請黜弼。」

translations.literal: The Vice Censor-in-Chief Han Jiang again said: "Zi ought not command troops, yet the chief councilor Fu Bi recommended and brought him forward — please dismiss Bi."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Han Jiang protested again: "Zi should not hold military command, yet Chief Councilor Fu Bi sponsored his appointment. I ask that Bi be removed."

sentences.zh: 弼引咎求罷政事。

translations.literal: Bi took blame upon himself and asked to be relieved of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bi accepted blame and asked to leave office.

sentences.zh: 諫官御史皆言進擬不自弼。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials and censors all said the nomination had not originated with Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials and censors alike said the nomination had not come from Bi.

sentences.zh: 絳家居待罪，曰：「不敢復稱御史矣。」

translations.literal: Jiang remained at home awaiting punishment and said: "I dare not call myself a censor again."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang stayed home awaiting punishment, saying, "I no longer dare call myself a censor."

sentences.zh: 坐此謫知蔡州。

translations.literal: For this he was demoted and made prefect of Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was demoted to prefect of Cai.

sentences.zh: 而孜尋以罪罷，知曹州。

translations.literal: Zi was soon dismissed for crime and made prefect of Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zi was soon removed for misconduct and appointed prefect of Cao.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉，諡勤惠。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Grand Marshal and given the posthumous title Qinhuai.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously enfeoffed as grand marshal with the temple name Qinhuai.

sentences.zh: 孜初名茂實，避英宗舊名，改「孜」云。

translations.literal: Zi was originally named Maoshi; to avoid the former personal name of Emperor Yingzong he changed it to "Zi," it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Zi had originally been named Maoshi; to avoid Emperor Yingzong's former personal name he changed it to Zi.

sentences.zh: 許懷德

translations.literal: Xu Huaide
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huaide

sentences.zh: 許懷德，字師古，開封祥符人。

translations.literal: Xu Huaide, courtesy name Shigu, was a man of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huaide, style name Shigu, came from Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父均，磁州團練使。

translations.literal: His father Jun was regimental commander of Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun served as regimental commander of Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 懷德長六尺餘，善騎射擊刺。

translations.literal: Huaide was over six feet tall and excelled at mounted archery and thrusting combat.
translations.idiomatic: Huaide stood more than six feet tall and was skilled in horsemanship, archery, and close combat.

sentences.zh: 少以父任為東西班殿侍，累擢至殿前指揮使、左班都虞候。

translations.literal: In youth, through his father's privilege, he became an attendant of the Eastern and Western Classes; he was promoted in succession to commander of the Palace Front Guard and chief commandant of the Left Class.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he entered service through his father's privilege as a palace attendant of the eastern and western classes, rising eventually to commander of the palace front guard and chief commandant of the left class.

sentences.zh: 元昊寇邊，選為儀州刺史、鄜延路兵馬鈐轄，遷副總管。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao raided the border, Huaide was selected as prefect of Yizhou and military inspector of the Fuyan Circuit, then promoted to deputy overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao attacked the frontier, Huaide was chosen prefect of Yizhou and military inspector on the Fuyan circuit, then promoted to deputy overall commander.

sentences.zh: 夏人三萬騎圍承平砦，懷德時在城中，率勁兵千餘人突圍，破之。

translations.literal: Thirty thousand Xia horsemen besieged Chengpu Stockade; Huaide was then in the city and led more than a thousand crack troops in a breakout and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When thirty thousand Xia cavalry besieged Chengpu Stockade, Huaide was inside the walls; he led over a thousand elite troops in a breakout and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 夏人復陣，有出陣前據鞍嫚罵者，懷德引弓一發而踣，敵乃去。

translations.literal: The Xia formed battle lines again; one man came before the ranks, sat on his saddle, and reviled them in contempt — Huaide drew his bow and with one shot felled him, and the enemy then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia re-formed their lines. One warrior rode forward, sat on his saddle, and hurled insults. Huaide loosed a single arrow and dropped him; the enemy then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 屠金明縣，復進圍延州。

translations.literal: They slaughtered Jinming County and again advanced to besiege Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: They sacked Jinming County and pressed on to besiege Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 懷德遽還，夜遣裨將以步騎千餘人，出不意擊之，斬首二百級，遂解延州。

translations.literal: Huaide hurried back and by night sent a lieutenant with more than a thousand infantry and cavalry to strike them unexpectedly; they took two hundred heads and thus lifted the siege of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huaide rushed back and that night sent a subordinate with over a thousand foot and horse to strike by surprise, taking two hundred heads and relieving Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遷鳳州團練使，專領延州東路茭村一帶公事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to regimental commander of Feng Prefecture, exclusively in charge of official business along the Jiaocun stretch of the eastern Yanzhou road.
translations.idiomatic: He was made regimental commander of Feng and given sole charge of affairs along the Jiaocun sector of Yanzhou's eastern route.

sentences.zh: 徙秦鳳路，未行，坐夏人破塞門砦不赴援，降寧州刺史。

translations.literal: He was shifted to the Qinfeng Circuit; before he departed, because the Xia had broken Saimen Stockade and he had not gone to relieve it, he was demoted to prefect of Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the Qinfeng circuit, he had not yet left when the Xia stormed Saimen Stockade without his going to the rescue; he was demoted to prefect of Ning.

sentences.zh: 頃之，擢龍神衛四廂都指揮使、陵州團練使、本路副都總管。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to overall commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, regimental commander of Ling Prefecture, and deputy overall commander of the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to commander of the dragon spirit guard's four wings, regimental commander of Ling, and deputy overall commander of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 遷康州防禦使，又坐當出討賊逗留不進，所部兵夫棄隨軍芻糧，更赦，徙秦鳳路副都總管，改捧日、天武四廂。

translations.literal: He was transferred to defender of Kang Prefecture; again, because when he should have gone out to attack bandits he lingered and did not advance and the laborers under his command abandoned the fodder grain that followed the army, after a further amnesty he was shifted to deputy overall commander of the Qinfeng Circuit and changed to the Penglai and Tianwu four wings.
translations.idiomatic: Made defender of Kang, he was punished again for delaying a campaign against bandits while his laborers abandoned the army's fodder. After another amnesty he became deputy overall commander on Qinfeng and was reassigned to the Penglai and Tianwu wings.

sentences.zh: 又以賊侵掠屬羌，亡十餘帳，徙永興軍，又徙高陽關、幷代路，歷殿前都虞候、遂州觀察使、侍衛親軍馬軍副都指揮使、武信軍節度觀察留後、殿前副都指揮使、寧遠軍節度使。

translations.literal: Again, because bandits raided dependent Qiang and more than ten tents were lost, he was shifted to Yongxing Army, then to Gaoyang Pass and the Bingdai Circuit, passing through chief commandant of the palace front, observation commissioner of Suizhou, deputy overall commander of the palace cavalry of the imperial guards, military commissioner and observation remnant of Wuxin Army, deputy overall commander of the palace front, and military commissioner of Ningyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders harried subject Qiang and more than ten camps were lost, he was moved to Yongxing Army, then Gaoyang Pass and the Bingdai circuit, serving in turn as palace front chief commandant, observation commissioner of Suizhou, deputy overall commander of the imperial guards cavalry, Wuxin military commissioner and observation remnant, deputy palace front commander, and military commissioner of Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 會從妹亡，無子，懷德欲冒有其田，事覺，罷管軍，知亳州，徙徐州。

translations.literal: It happened that a cousin on his mother's side died without a son; Huaide wished to seize her fields by false claim — when the matter came to light he was removed from troop command and made prefect of Bozhou, then shifted to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When a maternal cousin died childless, Huaide tried to seize her land by false claim. Exposed, he lost command of the guards and was made prefect of Bo, then transferred to Xu.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，復為殿前副都指揮使。

translations.literal: After more than a year he again became deputy overall commander of the palace front.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he again became deputy overall commander of the palace front.

sentences.zh: 祀明堂，進都指揮使，更保寧、建雄二節度。

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall was sacrificed to, he was advanced to overall commander and successively held the Ningbao and Jianxiong military commissions.
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall rites he was promoted to overall commander and in turn held the Ningbao and Jianxiong commissions.

sentences.zh: 年八十猶生子，筋力過人。

translations.literal: At eighty he still fathered a child; his sinew and strength surpassed ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: At eighty he still fathered a child, his strength surpassing that of ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 在宿衛十四年，數乞身，帝不許。

translations.literal: He was in palace guard service fourteen years and several times begged to retire; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the palace guards for fourteen years and repeatedly asked to retire; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 懷德曰：「臣年過矣，倘為御史所彈，且不得善罷。」

translations.literal: Huaide said: "Your servant's years are past — if censors impeach me, I may not be able to leave office with honor."
translations.idiomatic: Huaide said, "I am too old; if the censors attack me, I may not be allowed an honorable exit."

sentences.zh: 即詔為減數歲。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was ordered to have several years subtracted from his age.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered several years struck from his recorded age.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈侍中，諡榮毅。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Palace Attendant and given the posthumous title Rongyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made palace attendant with the temple name Rongyi.

sentences.zh: 懷德自初擢守邊，連以畏懦被謫，已而與功臣並進典軍，及坐請託得罪，去而復還。

translations.literal: From his first promotion to frontier defense Huaide was repeatedly demoted for timidity and cowardice, yet later he advanced with meritorious ministers to jointly command troops; when he was punished for solicitation he left and returned again.
translations.idiomatic: From his first frontier appointment Huaide was repeatedly demoted for cowardice, yet later rose with distinguished generals to high command; punished once for patronage, he left office and came back again.

sentences.zh: 時遭承平，保寵終祿。

translations.literal: The times met with enduring peace; he preserved favor and ended on salary.
translations.idiomatic: In an age of peace he kept imperial favor and died on his stipend.

sentences.zh: 故事，節度使移鎮加恩，皆別上表再辭，每降批答，遣內侍齎賜，必有所遺。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a military commissioner shifted garrison and received added favor, each submitted a separate memorial declining twice; each time an edict in reply was issued and an inner attendant was sent bearing gifts — there was always something bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when a commissioner changed posts and received new honors he filed a separate memorial declining twice; each time the throne answered and sent a palace eunuch with gifts, always with something extra.

sentences.zh: 懷德以祫享加恩，既又移鎮，乃共為一表以辭。

translations.literal: Huaide, for ancestral temple rites, received added favor; having again shifted garrison, he combined both into one memorial to decline.
translations.idiomatic: Huaide had received honors for ancestral rites and, on shifting posts again, rolled both into a single declining memorial.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士歐陽修劾其慢朝命，詔以修章示之，懷德謝罪而已，不復別進表。

translations.literal: Hanlin academician Ouyang Xiu impeached him for slighting court orders; the emperor ordered Xiu's memorial shown to him — Huaide apologized and that was all; he did not again submit a separate memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Ouyang Xiu charged him with disrespect for court procedure; the emperor had the memorial shown to him. Huaide apologized and submitted no further separate memorial.

sentences.zh: 其鄙吝如此。

translations.literal: He was this petty and stingy.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his pettiness and meanness.

sentences.zh: 李允則

translations.literal: Li Yunze
translations.idiomatic: Li Yunze

sentences.zh: 李允則，字垂範，濟州團練使謙溥子也。

translations.literal: Li Yunze, courtesy name Chuifan, was the son of Li Qianbo, regimental commander of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yunze, style name Chuifan, was the son of Jizhou regimental commander Li Qianbo.

sentences.zh: 少以材略聞，蔭補衙內指揮使，改左班殿直。

translations.literal: In youth he was known for talent and stratagem; by privilege he was appointed commander of the inner yamen and changed to left-class palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Known young for ability and strategy, he entered by privilege as inner-yamen commander and became a left-class palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 太平興國七年，幽薊還師，始置榷場於靜戎軍，允則典其事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo, when the army returned from You-Ji, the monopoly market was first established at Jingrong Army; Yunze managed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 7, when troops withdrew from You and Ji, the first border market was set at Jingrong Army; Yunze ran it.

sentences.zh: 還，使河東路決繫囚，原治逋欠。

translations.literal: On return he was sent to the Hedong Circuit to decide cases of bound prisoners and pardon overdue levies.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he was sent to Hedong to adjudicate bound prisoners and forgive overdue taxes.

sentences.zh: 又使荊湖察官吏，與轉運使檢視錢帛、器甲、刑獄，遂擢閤門祗候。

translations.literal: Again he was sent to Jinghu to inspect officials, and with the transport commissioner to examine cash, silks, armor, and prisons — then he was promoted to palace gate usher.
translations.idiomatic: He was next sent to Jinghu to inspect officials and, with the transport commissioner, review funds, arms, and prisons, and was promoted to palace gate usher.

sentences.zh: 浚治京師諸河，創水門，鄭州水磑。

translations.literal: He dredged the capital's rivers, created water gates, and the Zhengzhou water mill.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged the capital's waterways, built sluice gates, and established the Zhengzhou water mill.

sentences.zh: 西川賊劉旰平，上官正議修城未決，命允則與王承衎、閻承翰往視。

translations.literal: When the rebel Liu Chang of Xichuan was pacified, Shang Guanzheng debated whether to repair the walls but had not decided; the court ordered Yunze with Wang Chenghan and Yan Chenghan to go inspect.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Chang's rebellion in Xichuan was crushed, Shang Guanzheng had debated wall repairs without deciding; Yunze was sent with Wang Chenghan and Yan Chenghan to inspect.

sentences.zh: 還，言西川以無城難守，宜如正議。

translations.literal: On return he said that in Xichuan, without walls defense was hard, and the court should follow Zheng's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that Xichuan could not be held without walls and that Zheng's plan should be adopted.

sentences.zh: 又言兵分則緩急不為用，請亻並屯要害，以便饋餉。

translations.literal: He also said that if troops were divided they would not serve in urgency — he asked to mass them at strategic points to ease supply.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that scattered troops could not meet emergencies and asked to concentrate them at key points to ease logistics.

sentences.zh: 高溪州蠻田彥伊入寇，遣詣辰州，與轉運使張素、荊南劉昌言計事。

translations.literal: When the Gao-Xi Prefecture Man chief Tian Yanyi invaded, he was dispatched to Chen Prefecture to plan with Transport Commissioner Zhang Su and Jingnan's Liu Changyan.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Yanyi of the Gao-Xi Man raided, Yunze was sent to Chen to confer with Transport Commissioner Zhang Su and Liu Changyan of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 允則以蠻徼不足加兵，悉招輯之。

translations.literal: Yunze held that the Man frontier did not warrant added troops and entirely summoned and gathered them in.
translations.idiomatic: Yunze held the Man border did not need more troops and pacified them by summons and settlement.

sentences.zh: 累遷供備庫副使、知潭州。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to deputy commissioner of the supply depot and prefect of Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to deputy commissioner of the supply depot and prefect of Tan.

sentences.zh: 將行，真宗謂曰：「朕在南衙，畢士安嘗道卿家世，今以湖南屬卿。」

translations.literal: About to depart, Emperor Zhenzong said to him: "When I was in the Southern Yamen, Bi Shi'an once spoke of your family line — now I entrust Hunan to you."
translations.idiomatic: Before he left, Zhenzong said, "When I was heir apparent, Bi Shi'an spoke of your family; now I entrust Hunan to you."

sentences.zh: 初，馬氏暴斂，州人出絹，謂之地稅。

translations.literal: At first the Ma clan had levied harshly; the people paid silk called land tax.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ma clan the people had paid a "land tax" in silk from harsh exactions.

sentences.zh: 潘美定湖南，計屋輸絹，謂之屋稅。

translations.literal: When Pan Mei pacified Hunan, they assessed silk by dwelling called house tax.
translations.idiomatic: When Pan Mei pacified Hunan, silk was assessed per dwelling as "house tax."

sentences.zh: 營田戶給牛，歲輸米四斛，牛死猶輸，謂之枯骨稅。

translations.literal: Military colonists were given oxen and paid four hu of grain yearly; when the ox died they still paid — called dead-bone tax.
translations.idiomatic: Colonists given oxen paid four hu of grain yearly; even when the ox died they still paid—the "dead-bone tax."

sentences.zh: 民輸茶，初以九斤為一大斤，後益至三十五斤。

translations.literal: The people paid tea — at first nine jin made one large jin; later it increased to thirty-five jin.
translations.idiomatic: Tea levies had begun at nine jin to the "large jin" and risen to thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 允則請除三稅，茶以十三斤半為定制，民皆便之。

translations.literal: Yunze asked to abolish the three taxes and fix tea at thirteen and a half jin as the standard measure; the people all found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Yunze abolished the three taxes and fixed tea at thirteen and a half jin per standard measure, to the people's relief.

sentences.zh: 湖湘多山田，可以藝粟，而民惰不耕。

translations.literal: Hunan and Xiang had many mountain fields where millet could be grown, but the people were lazy and did not plow.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan had abundant hillside land for grain, but the people were idle and would not farm.

sentences.zh: 乃下令月所給馬芻，皆輸本色，繇是山田悉墾。

translations.literal: He then ordered that monthly horse fodder issued must be paid in kind — thereby mountain fields were all opened.
translations.idiomatic: He required monthly horse fodder to be paid in kind, and hillside fields were brought under cultivation.

sentences.zh: 湖南饑，欲發官廩先賑而後奏，轉運使執不可，允則曰：「須報逾月，則饑者無及矣。」

translations.literal: Hunan suffered famine; he wished to open government granaries to relieve first and report afterward — the transport commissioner insisted it could not be done; Yunze said: "To wait for report exceeds a month — then the starving will not be reached."
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Hunan he wanted to open granaries first and report later; the transport commissioner refused. Yunze said, "A month's delay in reporting means the hungry go unserved."

sentences.zh: 明年薦饑，復欲先賑，轉運使又執不可，允則請以家資為質，乃得發廩賤糶。

translations.literal: The next year famine was severe again; he again wished to relieve first — the transport commissioner again insisted it could not be done; Yunze asked to pledge his family wealth as surety and only then obtained permission to open granaries and sell grain cheap.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, famine again, he again sought to relieve first; blocked again, he pledged his personal wealth as bond and was allowed to sell grain cheap from the granaries.

sentences.zh: 因募饑民堪役者隸軍籍，得萬人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he recruited famine victims fit for service and enrolled them in the army rolls — ten thousand men were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: He then enrolled able-bodied famine victims in the army, gaining ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 轉運使請發所募兵禦邵州蠻，允則曰：「今蠻不攪，無名益戍，是長邊患也。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner asked to send the recruited troops against the Shao Prefecture Man; Yunze said: "Now the Man are not stirring — to reinforce without cause is to grow the border trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner wanted the new troops sent against the Shao Man; Yunze objected: "The tribes are quiet; pointless reinforcement only worsens the frontier.

sentences.zh: 且兵皆新募，饑瘠未任出戍。」

translations.literal: Moreover the troops were newly recruited — famished and lean, they were not fit to go on garrison duty."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, they were raw recruits, still thin from hunger, unfit for garrison duty."

sentences.zh: 乃奏罷之。

translations.literal: He then memorialized to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized and the deployment was canceled.

sentences.zh: 陳堯叟安撫湖南，民列允則治狀請留，堯叟以聞。

translations.literal: When Chen Yaosou pacified Hunan, the people listed Yunze's governance and asked that he remain; Yaosou reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Yaosou pacified Hunan, the people petitioned to keep Yunze; Yaosou reported it.

sentences.zh: 召還，連對三日，帝曰：「畢士安不謬知人者。」

translations.literal: Summoned back, he answered at audience three days in succession; the emperor said: "Bi Shi'an was not wrong to know men."
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he had three days of audiences; the emperor said, "Bi Shi'an knew his man."

sentences.zh: 遷洛苑副使、知滄州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy commissioner of the Luoyuan and prefect of Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became deputy commissioner of the Luoyuan and prefect of Cang.

sentences.zh: 允則巡視州境，浚浮陽湖，葺營壘，官舍間穿井。

translations.literal: Yunze toured the prefecture, dredged Fuyang Lake, repaired camps and offices, and sank wells between buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Touring his jurisdiction he dredged Fuyang Lake, repaired fortifications and offices, and dug wells among the buildings.

sentences.zh: 未幾，契丹來攻，老幼皆入保而水不乏，斫冰代砲，契丹遂解去。

translations.literal: Before long the Khitan came to attack; old and young all entered the forts and water did not run short; they chopped ice in place of catapult stones — the Khitan then lifted the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Khitan attacked; civilians took refuge inside and water held; defenders hurled chopped ice like catapult stones, and the Khitan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 真宗復召謂曰：「頃有言卿浚井葺屋為勞民者，及契丹至，始見善為備也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong again summoned him and said: "Recently some said you dredged wells and repaired houses to weary the people — when the Khitan came, one then saw you had prepared well."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong summoned him and said, "Some called your wells and repairs a burden on the people—until the Khitan came and showed how well you had prepared."

sentences.zh: 轉西上閤門副使、鎮定高陽三路行營兵馬都監，押大陣東面。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy chief of the Western Upper Palace Gate, overall military inspector of the three routes of Zhending and Gaoyang, and commander of the east face of the great array.
translations.idiomatic: He was made deputy chief of the western upper palace gate, overall military inspector of the Zhending-Gaoyang three routes, commanding the array's east face.

sentences.zh: 請對，自陳武藝非所長，不可以當邊劇。

translations.literal: He requested audience and confessed that martial skill was not his strength — he could not bear the border's severity.
translations.idiomatic: He asked audience and admitted martial skill was not his forte and he could not bear the frontier's strain.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿為我運籌策，不必當矢石也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You need only devise plans for Us — you need not face arrows and stones."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Plan for me—you need not stand under arrows and stones."

sentences.zh: 賜白金二千兩，副以幃幄、什器，凡下諸路宣敕，必先屬允則省而後行。

translations.literal: He was granted two thousand taels of white gold, with curtains, utensils, and the like; whenever edicts were issued to the circuits, they had first to pass through Yunze for review before execution.
translations.idiomatic: He received two thousand taels of silver plus tents and equipment; edicts to the circuits had to pass his review first.

sentences.zh: 及王超敗，人心震搖，允則勸超衰絰向師哭，以解眾忿。

translations.literal: When Wang Chao was defeated, hearts shook; Yunze urged Chao to wear mourning hemp and weep toward the army to dissolve the troops' anger.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Chao's defeat shook morale, Yunze urged him to wear mourning and weep before the troops to defuse their fury.

sentences.zh: 真宗知允則始屢趣超進兵，手詔褒厲。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong knew Yunze had repeatedly urged Chao to advance; by handwritten edict he praised and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Yunze had repeatedly pressed Chao to advance, Zhenzong sent a personal edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 契丹通好，徙知瀛州，上言：「朝廷已許契丹和議，但擇邊將，謹誓約，有言和好非利者，請一切斥去。」

translations.literal: When the Khitan made peace, he was shifted to prefect of Ying Prefecture and memorialized: "The court has already agreed peace with the Khitan — only choose border generals, keep the oath strictly, and whoever speaks that peace is not advantageous, please dismiss them all."
translations.idiomatic: At Khitan peace he became prefect of Ying and memorialized: "Choose good border commanders, keep the treaty, and dismiss anyone who says peace harms us."

sentences.zh: 真宗曰：「茲朕意也。」

translations.literal: Zhenzong said: "This is Our intent."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong said, "That is my intent."

sentences.zh: 遷西上閤門副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy chief of the Western Upper Palace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted deputy chief of the western upper palace gate.

sentences.zh: 何承矩為河北緣邊安撫、提點榷場，及承矩疾，詔自擇代，乃請允則知雄州。

translations.literal: He Chengjue was frontier pacification commissioner and monopoly-market intendant of Hebei; when Chengjue fell ill, the emperor ordered him to choose his own replacement — he then asked that Yunze be made prefect of Xiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When He Chengjue, Hebei frontier commissioner and market intendant, fell ill and was told to pick his successor, he named Yunze for Xiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，禁榷場遇異物，而邏者得所易瑉玉帶。

translations.literal: At first the monopoly market forbade unusual goods in trade, but a border man obtained a traded jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: Markets had barred exotic goods, yet a frontier trader acquired a jade belt in exchange.

sentences.zh: 允則曰：「此以我無用易彼有用也」，縱不治。

translations.literal: Yunze said: "This is exchanging what we do not need for what they need"; he let it pass without punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yunze said, "We trade our surplus for their need," and took no action.

sentences.zh: 遷東上閤門使、獎州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief of the Eastern Upper Palace Gate and prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief of the eastern upper palace gate and prefect of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 河北既罷兵，允則治城壘不輟，契丹主曰：「南朝尚修城備，得無違誓約乎？」

translations.literal: After Hebei had ceased hostilities, Yunze did not stop repairing walls and ramparts; the Khitan ruler said: "The Southern Court still repairs walls and preparations — can this not violate the oath?"
translations.idiomatic: With fighting ended in Hebei, Yunze kept fortifying; the Khitan ruler asked whether this broke the treaty.

sentences.zh: 其相張儉曰：「李雄州為安撫使，其人長者，不足疑。」

translations.literal: His councilor Zhang Jian said: "Li of Xiong Prefecture is the pacification commissioner — the man is upright and long-standing; he is not to be doubted."
translations.idiomatic: Councilor Zhang Jian replied, "Commissioner Li of Xiong is a man of integrity—not to be doubted."

sentences.zh: 既而有詔詰之，允則奏曰：「初通好不即完治，恐他日頹圮因此廢守，邊患不可測也。」

translations.literal: Then there was an edict questioning him; Yunze memorialized: "At the first peace we did not at once complete repairs, fearing that later collapse would for that reason abandon defense — border trouble cannot be measured."
translations.idiomatic: When the court questioned him, Yunze wrote: "We did not finish repairs at once lest later ruin force us to abandon the walls—frontier risk is incalculable."

sentences.zh: 帝以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor held it right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 城北舊有甕城，允則欲合大城為一。

translations.literal: North of the city there had been an urn city; Yunze wished to merge it with the great wall.
translations.idiomatic: North of the city lay an outer barbican; Yunze wanted to join it to the main wall.

sentences.zh: 先建東嶽祠，出黃金百兩為供器，道以鼓吹，居人爭獻金銀。

translations.literal: First he built the Eastern Peak temple, contributed a hundred taels of gold as offering vessels, and paraded with music — residents competed to offer gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: He first built an Eastern Peak temple, donated a hundred taels of gold for ritual vessels, and marched with music; townspeople vied to give gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 久之，密自徹去，聲言盜自北至，遂下令捕盜，三移文北界，乃興版築，揚言以護祠。

translations.literal: After a long while he secretly removed them and announced that thieves had come from the north; he then ordered the capture of thieves and three times sent documents to the northern border — only then began construction, proclaiming it was to protect the temple.
translations.idiomatic: He later secretly removed the gold and claimed northern thieves had struck; ordering a manhunt and thrice notifying the northern border, he began building, saying it was to guard the shrine.

sentences.zh: 而卒就關城浚壕，起月堤，自此甕城之人，悉內城中。

translations.literal: In the end he completed closing the wall and digging the moat, raising moon dikes — from this the people of the urn city all moved inside the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: He closed the wall, dug the moat, and raised crescent embankments until barbican dwellers all moved inside.

sentences.zh: 始，州民多以草覆屋，允則取材木西山，大為倉廩營舍。

translations.literal: At first the prefecture's people mostly roofed with thatch; Yunze took timber from the western hills and greatly built granaries and barracks.
translations.idiomatic: Most roofs had been thatch; Yunze brought timber from the western hills and built granaries and barracks on a large scale.

sentences.zh: 始教民陶瓦甓，標里閈，置廊市、邸舍、水磑。

translations.literal: He first taught the people to fire tile and brick, marked lanes and wards, and set colonnades, markets, inns, and water mills.
translations.idiomatic: He taught tile-making, laid out wards and markets, inns, and water mills.

sentences.zh: 城上悉累甓，下環以溝塹，蒔麻植榆柳。

translations.literal: On the wall he piled brick entirely; below he ringed moats and ditches and planted hemp, elm, and willow.
translations.idiomatic: The ramparts were fully tiled; moats encircled them, planted with hemp, elm, and willow.

sentences.zh: 廣閻承翰所修屯田，架石橋，構亭榭，列堤道，以通安肅、廣信、順安軍。

translations.literal: He broadened the military colonies Yan Chenghan had repaired, set stone bridges, built pavilions, and laid embankment roads to connect Ansu, Guangxin, and Shun'an Armies.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded Yan Chenghan's garrison farms, bridged streams, built pavilions, and linked Ansu, Guangxin, and Shun'an garrisons with raised roads.

sentences.zh: 歲修禊事，召界河戰棹為競渡，縱北人遊觀，潛寓水戰。

translations.literal: Each year he held the spring purification rite, summoned battle boats on the border river for racing, allowed northerners to watch — secretly training for river warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Each year he held spring rites and regatta on the border river, letting northerners watch while secretly drilling naval tactics.

sentences.zh: 州北舊多設陷馬坑，城上起樓為斥堠，望十里；

translations.literal: North of the prefecture many horse-trap pits had been set; on the wall towers were raised as watchposts, seeing ten li;
translations.idiomatic: North of the city lay many horse pits; watch towers on the walls commanded ten li of view;

sentences.zh: 自罷兵，人莫敢登。

translations.literal: since hostilities ceased, no one dared ascend.
translations.idiomatic: since the truce, no one had dared man them.

sentences.zh: 允則曰：「南北既講和矣，安用此為？」

translations.literal: Yunze said: "North and south have already made peace — what use is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yunze said, "North and south are at peace—what need for these?"

sentences.zh: 命徹樓夷坑，為諸軍蔬圃，浚井疏洫，列畦隴，築短垣，縱橫其中，植以荊棘，而其地益阻隘。

translations.literal: He ordered the towers dismantled and the pits leveled, made vegetable gardens for the armies, dug wells and cleared irrigation, laid out fields and ridges, built low walls crisscrossing within them planted with thorns — and the ground became all the more obstructive and narrow.
translations.idiomatic: He had the towers torn down and pits filled, turned the ground into army vegetable plots, dug wells and channels, laid fields behind low thorn hedges, and made the terrain still harder to cross.

sentences.zh: 因治坊巷，徙浮圖北原上，州民旦夕登望三十里，下令安撫司，所治境有隙地悉種榆，久之榆滿塞下。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered lanes repaired and moved the pagoda to the northern plateau — the prefecture's people morning and evening climbed to gaze thirty li; he ordered the pacification office that wherever there was spare land in the jurisdiction they should plant elm — before long elms filled the area below the pass.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt streets, moved a pagoda to the northern heights so townsfolk could scan thirty li, and ordered spare land planted with elm until the border was thick with trees.

sentences.zh: 顧謂僚佐曰：「此步兵之地，不利騎戰，豈獨資屋材耶？」

translations.literal: He turned to his aides and said: "This is infantry ground, unfavorable to cavalry battle — was it only for building timber?
translations.idiomatic: He told his staff, "This suits foot soldiers, not cavalry—was it only for lumber?"

sentences.zh: 上元舊不燃燈，允則結彩山，聚優樂，使民夜縱遊。

translations.literal: On the Lantern Festival lamps had not been lit in the past; Yunze erected a brocade mountain, gathered actors and musicians, and let the people roam at night.
translations.idiomatic: Lantern Festival lights had been forbidden; Yunze built a decorated mountain, hired performers, and let the people celebrate at night.

sentences.zh: 明日，偵知北酋欲間入城中觀，允則與同僚伺郊外。

translations.literal: The next day, scouts learned the northern chief wished to slip into the city to observe; Yunze with his colleagues waited in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Next day intelligence said the Khitan leader meant to enter the city in disguise; Yunze and colleagues waited outside.

sentences.zh: 果有紫衣人至，遂與俱入傳舍，不交一言，出奴女羅侍左右，劇飲而罷。

translations.literal: Indeed a man in purple came; Yunze went with him into the relay lodge, exchanged not a word, produced slave girls to attend left and right, and drank heavily before parting.
translations.idiomatic: A man in purple arrived; Yunze escorted him to the guesthouse, said nothing, set slave girls to serve wine, and drank him under the table.

sentences.zh: 且置其所乘騾廡下，使遁去，即幽州統軍也。

translations.literal: Meanwhile he placed the mule the man had ridden in the stable corridor and let him escape — it was the overall commander of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He stabled the visitor's mule and let him slip away—it was Youzhou's supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 後數日，為契丹所誅。

translations.literal: Several days later he was executed by the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the Khitan executed him.

sentences.zh: 嘗宴軍中，而甲仗庫火，允則作樂行酒不輟，副使請救，不答。

translations.literal: Once feasting in camp, the armory caught fire; Yunze kept music and wine going without pause — the deputy commissioner asked to fight the fire but received no answer.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a camp feast the armory burned; Yunze kept the music playing while his deputy begged to fight the flames in vain.

sentences.zh: 少頃火熄，命悉瘞所焚物，密遣吏持檄瀛州，以茗籠運器甲。

translations.literal: Before long the fire died; he ordered all burned goods buried, secretly sent clerks with documents to Ying Prefecture, and had tea chests transport arms and armor.
translations.idiomatic: When the fire died he buried the ruins, secretly requisitioned arms from Ying packed in tea chests.

sentences.zh: 不浹旬，兵數已完，人無知者。

translations.literal: Within ten days troop numbers were complete again and no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days stores were full again, unnoticed.

sentences.zh: 樞密院請劾不救火狀，真宗曰：「允則必有謂，姑詰之。」

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs asked to impeach him for not fighting the fire; Zhenzong said: "Yunze must have had a reason — for now question him."
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs moved to impeach him for not fighting the fire; Zhenzong said, "Yunze must have had his reasons—question him first."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「兵械所藏，儆火甚嚴，方宴而焚，必奸人所為。

translations.literal: He replied: "Where arms are stored, warnings against fire are very strict — to burn during a feast must be the work of traitors.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The armory is fire-hardened; a blaze during a feast must be sabotage.

sentences.zh: 舍宴而救，事或不測。」

translations.literal: To leave the feast to rescue — the affair might become unpredictable."
translations.idiomatic: To break off the feast might have caused worse trouble."

sentences.zh: 允則不事威儀，間或步出，遇民可語者，延坐與語，以是洞知人情。

translations.literal: Yunze did not trouble with ceremony; sometimes he walked out and, meeting people he could speak with, invited them to sit and talk — thus he thoroughly knew popular sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Ignoring pomp, he walked among the people, sat and talked with whomever he met, and knew the mood of the realm.

sentences.zh: 訟至，無大小面訊立斷。

translations.literal: When lawsuits came, great or small he questioned face to face and decided on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: He heard every suit in person, great or small, and judged at once.

sentences.zh: 善撫士卒，皆得其用。

translations.literal: He was good at comforting soldiers — all were put to use.
translations.idiomatic: He won his soldiers' loyalty and used them well.

sentences.zh: 盜發輒獲，人亦莫知所由。

translations.literal: When thieves acted they were always caught, yet people also never knew how.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves were always caught, though none knew how.

sentences.zh: 身無兼衣，食無重羞，不畜資財。

translations.literal: He had no spare coat, no duplicate dish at meals, and hoarded no wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He owned one coat, one plate at table, and no savings.

sentences.zh: 在河北二十餘年，事功最多，其方略設施，雖寓於遊觀、亭傳間，後人亦莫敢隳。

translations.literal: In Hebei more than twenty years, his achievements were the most — his stratagems, though lodged in sightseeing and relay pavilions, later men also dared not destroy.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years in Hebei brought his greatest deeds; even measures hidden in festivals and inns later generations dared not undo.

sentences.zh: 至於國信往來，費用儀式，多所裁定。

translations.literal: As for diplomatic missions coming and going, expenses and ritual forms — he settled many.
translations.idiomatic: He standardized much of the cost and ceremony of diplomatic traffic.

sentences.zh: 晚年居京師，有自契丹亡歸者，皆命舍允則家。

translations.literal: In his later years living in the capital, those who fled from the Khitan were all ordered housed at Yunze's home.
translations.idiomatic: In old age at court he sheltered every Khitan defector in his own house.

sentences.zh: 允則死，始寓樞密院大程官營。

translations.literal: When Yunze died, they were first lodged in the Bureau of Military Affairs' large relay barracks.
translations.idiomatic: After his death they were moved to the Bureau's guest quarters.

sentences.zh: 張亢，字公壽，自言後唐河南尹全義七世孫。

translations.literal: Zhang Kang, courtesy name Gongshou, said of himself that he was a seventh-generation descendant of Quanyi, Henan military governor under Later Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kang, style name Gongshou, claimed descent from Later Tang's Henan governor Quanyi, seven generations removed.

sentences.zh: 家於臨濮。

translations.literal: His family settled at Linpu.
translations.idiomatic: His family lived at Linpu.

sentences.zh: 少豪邁有奇節，事兄奎甚謹。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and lofty with unusual integrity and served his elder brother Kui very respectfully.
translations.idiomatic: Young, he was daring and principled and served his elder brother Kui with devotion.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，為廣安軍判官、應天府推官。

translations.literal: Having passed the jinshi examination, he became judicial officer of Guang'an Army and investigating officer of Yingtian Prefecture.
