translations.idiomatic: A jinshi graduate, he served as Guang'an Army judge and Yingtian investigating officer.

sentences.zh: 治白沙、石梁二渠，民無水患。

translations.literal: He managed the Baisha and Shiliang canals — the people had no water trouble.
translations.idiomatic: He managed the Baisha and Shiliang canals and ended flooding for the people.

sentences.zh: 改大理寺丞、簽書西京判官事。

translations.literal: He was changed to director of the Court of Judicial Review and recorder of the Western Capital's administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became a director of the Court of Judicial Review and recorder at the western capital.

sentences.zh: 通判鎮戎軍，上言：「趙德明死，其子元昊喜誅殺，勢必難制，宜亟防邊。」

translations.literal: As transit intendant of Zhenrong Army he memorialized: "Zhao Deming is dead; his son Yuan Hao delights in executions and killings — the situation will surely be hard to control; the border should be guarded urgently."
translations.idiomatic: As intendant at Zhenrong he warned: "Deming is dead and Yuan Hao loves killing; the frontier must be secured at once."

sentences.zh: 因論西北攻守之計，章數十上，仁宗欲用之，會丁母憂。

translations.literal: Thereupon he discussed northwest attack-and-defense plans — memorials numbering in the tens went up; Emperor Renzong wished to use him, but then he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He sent dozens of memorials on northwest defense; Renzong meant to employ him, but mourning for his mother intervened.

sentences.zh: 既而契丹聚兵幽、涿間，河北增備，遂起為如京使、知安肅軍。

translations.literal: Before long the Khitan massed troops between You and Zhuo; Hebei increased preparations — he was then raised to palace envoy and made prefect of Ansu Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan gathered at You and Zhuo and Hebei mobilized, he was recalled as palace envoy and prefect of Ansu.

sentences.zh: 因入對曰：「契丹歲享金帛甚厚，今其主孱而歲歉，懼中國見伐，特張言耳，非其實也。

translations.literal: Entering audience he said: "The Khitan yearly enjoy gold and silk in great measure; now their ruler is weak and the year is lean — they fear China will attack and merely bluster — it is not real.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he said the Khitan lived on Song tribute; their weak ruler and bad harvest made their threats empty.

sentences.zh: 萬一倍約，臣請擐甲為諸軍先。」

translations.literal: Should they break the treaty, your servant asks to don armor and lead the armies.
translations.idiomatic: If they break faith, I will arm first and lead the van."

sentences.zh: 元昊反，為涇原路兵馬鈐轄、知渭州，累遷右騏驥使、忠州刺史，徙鄜延路、知鄜州。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao rebelled, he became military inspector of the Jingyuan Circuit and prefect of Wei Prefecture, promoted in succession to right Qiji envoy and prefect of Zhong Prefecture, shifted to the Fuyan Circuit and prefect of Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao rebelled he became Jingyuan military inspector and Wei prefect, then Zhong prefect, then Fuyan inspector and Fu prefect.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized:

sentences.zh: 「舊制，諸路總管、鈐轄、都監各不過三兩員，餘官雖高，止不過一路。

translations.literal: "By old regulation, overall commanders, military inspectors, and chief supervisors on each circuit were each no more than two or three officers; other offices though high held no more than one circuit.
translations.idiomatic: "Formerly each route had at most two or three overall commanders, inspectors, and supervisors; higher titles did not multiply commands.

sentences.zh: 總管、鈐轄不預本路事。

translations.literal: Overall commanders and military inspectors did not intervene in the circuit's own affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Overall commanders and inspectors did not meddle in routine circuit business.

sentences.zh: 今每路多至十四五員，少亦不減十員，皆兼本路分事，不相統制，凡有論議，互報不同。

translations.literal: Now each circuit has as many as fourteen or fifteen, never fewer than ten — all concurrently handle the circuit's divided affairs without unified command; whenever there is discussion, mutual reports differ.
translations.idiomatic: Now each route has ten to fifteen officers sharing duties without a single chain of command, so orders conflict.

sentences.zh: 按唐總管，統軍，都統，處置、制置使，各有副貳，國朝亦有經略、排陣使，請約故事，別置使名，每路軍馬事，止以三兩員領之。

translations.literal: Examining Tang overall commanders, army commanders, army overall commanders, disposition and arrangement commissioners — each had deputies; our dynasty also had frontier and battle-array commissioners — please follow precedent and separately set commissioner titles so that each circuit's military horses and affairs are led by only two or three officers.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and early Song precedents had deputies and frontier commissioners; restore clear titles so two or three men lead each route's forces.

sentences.zh: 又涇原一路，自總管、鈐轄、都監、巡檢及城砦所部六十餘所，兵多者數千人，少者才千人，兵勢既分，不足以當大敵。

translations.literal: Again, on the Jingyuan route alone, from overall commander, military inspector, chief supervisor, and inspectors to stockades under command — more than sixty posts — where troops were many there were several thousand, where few only a thousand; military strength being divided is insufficient to meet a great enemy.
translations.idiomatic: On Jingyuan alone sixty-odd posts split forces of one to several thousand—too weak against a major invasion.

sentences.zh: 若敵以萬人為二十隊，多張聲勢以綴我軍，後以三五萬人大入奔突，則何以支？

translations.literal: If the enemy with ten thousand men forms twenty companies, greatly spreading clamor to pin our army, then afterward with thirty to fifty thousand men makes a great inrush and charge — how can we sustain it?
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy feints with twenty squads then hits with thirty or fifty thousand, how do we hold?

sentences.zh: 又比來主將與軍伍移易不定，人馬強弱，配屬未均。

translations.literal: Moreover, recently chief generals and army ranks have shifted without fixity — men and horses strong or weak, assignments not equal.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders and units shift constantly; strong and weak troops are unevenly assigned.

sentences.zh: 今涇原正兵五萬，弓箭手二萬，鄜延正兵不減六七萬，若能預為團結，明定節制，迭為應援，以逸待勞，則烏合饑餒之眾，豈能窺我淺深乎？

translations.literal: Now Jingyuan has fifty thousand regular troops and twenty thousand archers; Fuyan regulars are no less than sixty or seventy thousand — if we can beforehand form regiments, clearly fix command, and relay support in turn, waiting with ease for their labor — then a mob hungry and famished, can they probe our depth?
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan has fifty thousand regulars and twenty thousand archers; Fuyan sixty or seventy thousand—pre-formed regiments, clear command, and mutual relief could defeat hungry rabble.

sentences.zh: 請下韓琦、范仲淹分按，逐路以馬步軍八千已上至萬人，擇才位兼高者為總領。

translations.literal: Please send Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan to inspect by circuit; on each route choose from eight thousand foot and horse up to ten thousand, selecting those of highest talent and rank as overall leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Send Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan to assign eight to ten thousand troops per route under the ablest senior commanders.

sentences.zh: 其下分為三將：一為前鋒，一為策前鋒，一為後陣。

translations.literal: Below them divide into three generals: one vanguard, one to support the vanguard, one rear array.
translations.idiomatic: Under each, three generals: vanguard, vanguard reserve, and rear.

sentences.zh: 每將以使臣、忠佐三兩人，分屯要害之地，敵小入則一將出，大入則大將出。

translations.literal: Each general with two or three envoy-officers and loyal aides divides garrison at strategic places — small enemy entry one general goes out; large entry the great general goes out.
translations.idiomatic: Each general with aides holds key points—small raids meet one general, large ones the chief.

sentences.zh: 又量敵數多少，使鄰路出兵應接，此所謂常山蛇勢也。

translations.literal: Again measure enemy numbers and have neighboring circuits send troops in response — this is the so-called Constant Mountain serpent formation.
translations.idiomatic: Scale response to enemy strength and coordinate neighboring routes—the 'Constant Mountain serpent' deployment.

sentences.zh: 今萬人已上為一大將，一路又有主帥，延州領三大將，鄜州一大將，保安軍及西路巡檢、德靖砦共為一大將，則鄜延路兵五萬人矣。

translations.literal: Now ten thousand and above make one great general; one circuit also has a chief commander — Yan Prefecture leads three great generals, Fu Prefecture one great general, Bao'an Army and western-route inspectors and Dejing Stockade together one great general — then the Fuyan circuit has fifty thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Today ten thousand men per 'great general' fragments Fuyan's fifty thousand among Yan, Fu, Bao'an, and Dejing commands.

sentences.zh: 原渭州、鎮戎軍各一大將，渭州山外及瓦亭各一大將，則涇原路五萬人矣。

translations.literal: Formerly Wei Prefecture and Zhenrong Army each one great general; outside the mountains at Wei and Wating each one great general — then the Jingyuan circuit has fifty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan's fifty thousand should cluster under Wei, Zhenrong, Wating, and mountain posts—not scattered titular generals.

sentences.zh: 弓箭手、熟戶不在焉。

translations.literal: Archers and registered households are not included therein.
translations.idiomatic: Archers and allied tribes are extra.

sentences.zh: 昨延州之敗，蓋由諸將自守不相應援。

translations.literal: The defeat at Yan Prefecture yesterday — it was entirely because the generals each held their ground and did not mutually support.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou fell because generals refused to support each other.

sentences.zh: 請令邊臣預定其法，敵寇某所，則某將為先鋒，某將出某所為奇兵，某將出某所為聲援，某城砦相近出敢戰死士某所設覆，都、同巡檢則各扼要害。

translations.literal: Please order frontier ministers beforehand to fix the method: enemy raids a place — which general is vanguard, which issues from where as odd troops, which from where as vocal support, which nearby stockade sends dare-to-die men to where to set ambush — chief and joint inspectors each choke key points.
translations.idiomatic: Pre-assign who leads, who ambushes, who reinforces, and which stockades sortie when the enemy strikes a given point.

sentences.zh: 又令鄰路取某路出應，仍潛用旗幟為號。

translations.literal: Again order neighboring circuits which route to send response, still secretly using banners and flags as signals.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring routes should answer with agreed banner signals.

sentences.zh: 昨劉平救延州，前鋒陷賊者已二千騎，平猶不知。

translations.literal: When Liu Ping rescued Yan Prefecture, the vanguard trapped by the enemy was already two thousand horse — Ping still did not know.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanzhou Liu Ping never knew two thousand of his vanguard were already trapped.

sentences.zh: 趙瑜部馬軍間道先進，而趙振與王逵趨塞門，至高頭平路，白馬報敵張青蓋駐山東，振麾兵掩襲，乃瑜也。

translations.literal: Zhao Yu's cavalry detachment advanced first by a side path, while Zhao Zhen and Wang Kui hurried to Saimen — reaching Gaotou level road, a white horse reported the enemy with green canopy stationed east of the mountain; Zhen waved troops to strike by surprise — it was Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yu's cavalry took a side road while Zhao Zhen mistook him for the enemy on the Gaotou plain and attacked his own man.

sentences.zh: 臣在山外策應，未嘗用本指揮旗號，自以五行支干別為引旗。

translations.literal: Your servant, supporting from outside the mountains, never used this command's flags and signals — personally used the Five Phases and stems and branches separately as guide banners.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the mountains I never used standard signals but private banners keyed to the sexagenary cycle.

sentences.zh: 若甲子日本軍相遇，則先見者張青旗，後見者以緋旗應之，此是干相生，其干相克及支相生克亦如之。

translations.literal: If on a jiazi day our army met, the first seen raised a green banner, the later a crimson banner in response — this is stem mutual generation; stem mutual overcoming and branch generation and overcoming are likewise.
translations.idiomatic: On a jiazi day the first party raised green, the second crimson—stems and branches coded friend from foe.

sentences.zh: 蓋兵馬出入，晝則百步之外不能相知，若不預為之號，必誤軍事。

translations.literal: For horse and foot going in and out, by day beyond a hundred paces they cannot know each other — if signals are not fixed beforehand, military affairs will surely go wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond a hundred paces troops cannot recognize friends; without preset signals disaster follows.

sentences.zh: 國家承平日久，失於訓練，今每指揮藝精者不過百餘人，餘皆瘦弱不可用。

translations.literal: The state has long enjoyed peace and has failed in training — now in each command those skilled in arts are no more than a hundred-odd; the rest are frail and weak and unusable.
translations.idiomatic: Peace has rotted training; barely a hundred men per unit are fit.

sentences.zh: 且官軍所恃者，步軍與強弩爾。

translations.literal: Moreover what the government army relies on is foot soldiers and powerful crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: The army depends on infantry and heavy crossbows.

sentences.zh: 臣知渭州日，見廣勇軍廣弩者三百五十人，引一石二斗者僅百人，餘僅及七八斗，正欲閱習時易為力爾。

translations.literal: When your servant was prefect of Wei Prefecture, he saw among the Guangyong Army's powerful crossbowmen three hundred fifty — those drawing one shi two dou were barely a hundred; the rest reached only seven or eight dou — precisely because at review time it was easy to exert force.
translations.idiomatic: At Wei I found only a hundred of three hundred fifty Guangyong crossbowmen could draw full weight—most cheated on drill day.

sentences.zh: 臣以跳鐙弩試，皆不能張，閱習十餘日，裁得百餘人。

translations.literal: Your servant tested with jumping-stirrup crossbows — none could draw; after more than ten days of review barely a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Stirrup-drawn bows failed; ten days' drill yielded a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 又教以小坐法，亦十餘日，又教以帶甲小坐法，五十餘日始能服熟。

translations.literal: Again taught the small-sitting method — again more than ten days; again taught armored small-sitting — fifty-odd days before they could wear it skillfully.
translations.idiomatic: Small-sitting and armored drills took fifty days to master.

sentences.zh: 若安前弊以應新敵，其有必勝之理乎？

translations.literal: If we embrace old abuses to meet a new enemy — is there necessarily logic of certain victory?
translations.idiomatic: Old habits against a new foe guarantee no victory.

sentences.zh: 又兵官務張邊事，以媒進邀賞，劉平之敗，正繇貪功輕進，鎮戎軍最近賊境，每報賊騎至，不問多寡，凡主兵者皆出，至邊壕則賊已去矣。

translations.literal: Again military officers strive to inflate border affairs, using agents to advance and invite rewards — Liu Ping's defeat was precisely from greedy achievement and light advance; Zhenrong Army is nearest the bandit border — whenever bandit cavalry arrive, regardless of few or many, whoever commands troops all go out — reaching the border moat the bandits have already left.
translations.idiomatic: Officers court glory and advance rashly—Ping's defeat; at Zhenrong every alarm sends commanders to the moat after the enemy has left.

sentences.zh: 蓋權均勢埒，各不相下，若不出，則恐得怯懦之罪。

translations.literal: Authority equal and power matched, each unwilling to be below the other — if they do not go out, they fear the crime of cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: Rivals dare not stay in camp lest they be called cowards.

sentences.zh: 且諸路騎兵不能馳險，計其芻粟，一馬之費，可養步軍五人。

translations.literal: Moreover on all circuits cavalry cannot gallop rough terrain; counting their fodder grain, one horse's expense can feed five foot soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry cannot ride rough ground; one horse feeds five foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 馬高不及格，宜悉還坊監，止留十之三，餘以步兵代之。

translations.literal: Horses above height standard should all be returned to stud farms — only a third kept; the rest replaced with foot soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Return undersized horses to stud farms, keep a third, replace the rest with infantry.

sentences.zh: 又比來禁衛隊長，繇年勞換前班者，或為諸司使副，白丁試武技，亦命以官，而諸路弓箭手生長邊陲，父祖效命，累世捍賊，乃無進擢之路，何以激勸邊民？

translations.literal: Moreover recently palace guard squad leaders, through years of service exchanged to the forward class, become various bureau deputy commissioners; raw youths tested in martial arts also receive office — yet on all circuits archers grown on the frontier, fathers and grandfathers having served, generations defending bandits, have no path of promotion — how encourage border people?
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards win civil posts while frontier archers whose families fought for generations have no promotion—how motivate the border?

sentences.zh: 竊聞大帥議五路進師，且有用兵以來，屢出無功，若一旦深入，臣切以為未可也。

translations.literal: Your servant hears the great commander discusses five-route advance — moreover since troops were used, repeated sorties have been without achievement; if one day they advance deep, your servant deeply holds it cannot yet be done.
translations.idiomatic: I hear talk of a five-route invasion; repeated failures show deep penetration is premature.

sentences.zh: 山界諸州城砦，距邊止二三百里，夏兵器甲雖精利，其鬥戰不及山界部族，而財糧又盡出山界。

translations.literal: Stockades of prefectures within the mountain line are only two or three hundred li from the border — Xia weapons and armor though refined and sharp, their battle is not equal to mountain-line tribes, and finances and grain all come from outside the mountain line.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain stockades sit two or three hundred li from the border; Xia arms are fine but their fighters and supplies depend on the frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 若十月後令諸將分番出界，使夏人不得耕牧。

translations.literal: If after the tenth month we order generals in rotation to cross the border, the Xia people cannot plow and pasture.
translations.idiomatic: After the tenth month rotate raids across the border to deny Xia pasture and plowing.

sentences.zh: 然後出步兵，負十日糧，人日給米一升，馬日給粟四升、草五分，賊界有草地，以半資放牧，亦可減免運之半。

translations.literal: Then send out foot soldiers carrying ten days' grain — men daily one sheng of rice, horses daily four sheng of grain and five fen of fodder; within the bandit border there is grassland — use half to pasture, and transport can also be halved.
translations.idiomatic: Then march infantry with ten days' rations—men one sheng rice, horses four sheng grain—and graze half the horses in enemy grass to halve convoys.

sentences.zh: 王師既行，使唃廝囉及九姓回紇分制其後，必蕩覆巢穴。」

translations.literal: When royal troops march, send Gusiluo and the Nine Surname Uyghurs to divide and control their rear — surely they will overturn the nest.
translations.idiomatic: Let Gusiluo and the Nine-Clan Uyghurs strike the rear and the Xia nest will fall."

sentences.zh: 又言：「陝西民調發之苦，數倍常歲，宜一切權罷，令安撫司與逐州長吏減省他役，專應邊須。

translations.literal: He also said: "Shaanxi people's conscript labor pains are several times the normal year — please entirely suspend by temporary order, let the pacification office with each prefecture's senior officials reduce other corvée and exclusively meet border needs.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged suspending Shaanxi's multiplied levies so pacification offices could cut other labor and fund the frontier.

sentences.zh: 及選殿侍軍將各三十人，以駝、騾各二百，留其半河中，以運鄜、延、保安軍軍須，其半留乾州或永興軍，以運環、慶、原、渭、鎮戎軍軍須，分一轉運使專董其事。

translations.literal: And select thirty palace attendants and army generals each, with two hundred camels and mules each — keep half at Hezhong to transport Fuyan, Bao'an Army needs, half at Qian Prefecture or Yongxing Army to transport Huan, Qing, Yuan, Wei, Zhenrong needs — appoint one transport commissioner solely to supervise the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Pick thirty guards and generals each, two hundred camels and mules, split between Hezhong and Qianzhou to supply eastern and western routes under one transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又鄜州四路半當衝要，嘗以閑慢路遞鋪兵卒之半，貼衝要二路。

translations.literal: Again the four Fu Prefecture routes half lie on critical points — they often took half the relay-post soldiers of idle circuits and attached them to the two critical routes.
translations.idiomatic: Half of Fu's four routes are critical; shift idle relay troops to the busy lines.

sentences.zh: 驛百人，每三人挽小車，載二百五十斤至三百斤，若團亻並輦運，邊計亦未至失備，而民力可以寬矣。」

translations.literal: At relay stations a hundred men — every three men pull a small cart, loading two hundred fifty to three hundred jin — if regimented and combined for transport, border planning also will not reach loss of preparedness, and popular strength can be eased.
translations.idiomatic: Three men per cart at two hundred fifty jin, if convoyed in groups, keeps the border ready while easing the people's burden."

sentences.zh: 初，亢請乘驛入對，詔令手疏上之，後多施用。

translations.literal: At first Kang asked to enter audience by relay post; the emperor ordered him to submit in handwritten memorial — later much was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Kang had asked to rush to court; ordered to write instead, much of his plan was adopted.

sentences.zh: 進西上閤門使，改都鈐轄，屯延州。

translations.literal: He was advanced to deputy chief of the Western Upper Palace Gate, changed to overall military inspector, garrisoned at Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted deputy western palace gate chief and overall inspector, he garrisoned Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 又奏邊機軍政措置失宜者十事，言：

translations.literal: Again he memorialized ten matters where frontier opportunity and military government arrangement were improper, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He listed ten frontier military failures:

sentences.zh: 「王師每出不利，豈非節制不立，號令不明，訓練不至，器械不精？

translations.literal: "Whenever royal troops sortie they are unlucky — is it not that command is not established, orders not clear, training not reached, weapons not refined?
translations.idiomatic: "Every campaign fails from broken command, unclear orders, poor training, or bad arms—or

sentences.zh: 或中敵詭計，或自我貪功；

translations.literal: Or falling for enemy stratagem, or from our own greed for achievement;
translations.idiomatic: enemy tricks or our own greed;

sentences.zh: 或左右前後自不相救，或進退出入未知其便；

translations.literal: Or left, right, front, rear not saving each other, or advance, retreat, exit, entry not knowing convenience;
translations.idiomatic: wings that do not help, maneuvers misunderstood;

sentences.zh: 或兵多而不能用，或兵少而不能避；

translations.literal: Or many troops but unable to use them, or few troops but unable to avoid;
translations.idiomatic: too many men unused or too few to escape;

sentences.zh: 或為持權者所逼，或因懦將所牽；

translations.literal: Or compelled by those who hold power, or dragged by cowardly generals;
translations.idiomatic: pressure from superiors or cowardly subordinates;

sentences.zh: 或人馬困饑而不能奮，或山川險阻而不能通：此皆將不知兵之弊也。

translations.literal: Or men and horses hungry and weary and unable to strive, or mountains and rivers dangerous and narrow and unable to pass — these are all the faults of generals who do not know war.
translations.idiomatic: starved troops or impassable terrain—generals who do not know war.

sentences.zh: 未聞深究致敗之由而為之措置，徒益兵馬，未見勝術。

translations.literal: Not hearing deep inquiry into causes of defeat to make arrangements — merely adding horse and foot, not seeing winning methods.
translations.idiomatic: We add troops without studying why we lose.

sentences.zh: 一也。

translations.literal: First.
translations.idiomatic: First.

sentences.zh: 去春敵至延州，諸路發援兵，而河東、秦鳳各逾千里，涇原、環慶不減十程。

translations.literal: Last spring the enemy reached Yan Prefecture; all circuits sent relief troops — Hedong and Qinfeng each over a thousand li, Jingyuan and Huanqing no less than ten stages.
translations.idiomatic: Last spring at Yanzhou relief came a thousand li from Hedong and Qinfeng, ten stages from Jingyuan and Huanqing.

sentences.zh: 去秋賊出鎮戎，遠自鄜延發兵，千里遠鬥，銳氣已衰，如賊已退，乃是空勞師徒，異時更寇別路，必又如此，是謂不戰而自弊。

translations.literal: Last autumn bandits came out at Zhenrong — far from Fuyan troops were sent, a thousand li to distant battle, sharp spirit already decayed; if bandits had already withdrawn, it was empty labor of army and master — another time if bandits raid another route, it will again be thus — this is called not fighting yet harming oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Last autumn Fuyan marched a thousand li to Zhenrong after the enemy left—next raid, same waste: defeat without fighting.

sentences.zh: 二也。

translations.literal: Second.
translations.idiomatic: Second.

sentences.zh: 今鄜延副都總管許懷德兼管勾環慶軍馬，環慶副總管王仲寶復兼鄜延，其涇原、秦鳳總管等亦兼鄰路，雖令互相策應，然環州至延州十四五驛，徑赴亦不下十驛；

translations.literal: Now Fuyan deputy overall commander Xu Huaide concurrently manages Huanqing horse and foot; Huanqing deputy overall commander Wang Zhongbao again concurrently Fuyan — likewise Jingyuan and Qinfeng overall commanders also concurrently neighbor circuits; though ordered to plan mutual response, yet from Huan Prefecture to Yan Prefecture is fourteen or fifteen relay stages, going direct is also no less than ten stages;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huaide commands both Fuyan and Huanqing; Wang Zhongbao both Huanqing and Fuyan—cross-commands span ten to fifteen stages.

sentences.zh: 涇原至秦鳳千里，若發兵互援，而山路險惡，人馬之力已竭。

translations.literal: Jingyuan to Qinfeng a thousand li — if troops are sent to mutual aid, mountain roads are dangerous and harsh, men and horses' strength is already exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan to Qinfeng is a thousand li of brutal mountain marches that exhaust men and horses.

sentences.zh: 三也。

translations.literal: Third.
translations.idiomatic: Third.

sentences.zh: 四路軍馬各不下五六萬，朝廷罄力供億，而邊臣但言兵少，每路欲更增十萬人，亦未見功效。

translations.literal: Four circuits' troops are each no less than fifty or sixty thousand — the court exhausts strength to supply them, yet frontier ministers only say troops are few; each circuit wishes to add another hundred thousand — achievement is also not seen.
translations.idiomatic: Each route has fifty or sixty thousand men at imperial expense, yet officers demand another hundred thousand without results.

sentences.zh: 且兵無節制一弊，無奇正二弊，無應援三弊，主將不一四弊，兵分勢弱五弊。

translations.literal: Moreover troops without command one fault, without odd and orthodox two faults, without mutual relief three faults, chief generals not one four faults, troops divided and strength weak five faults.
translations.idiomatic: No unified command, no regular and irregular tactics, no mutual aid, divided leadership, and scattered strength—five fatal flaws.

sentences.zh: 有此五弊，如驅市人而戰，雖有百萬，亦無益於事。

translations.literal: Having these five faults, like driving market folk to war — though there be a million, it also does not benefit the affair.
translations.idiomatic: With these five flaws a million men fight like a mob.

sentences.zh: 四也。

translations.literal: Fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth.

sentences.zh: 古人教習，須三年而後成，今之用兵已三年矣，將帥之材孰賢孰愚，攻守之術孰得孰失，累年敗衄，而居邊要者未知何謀。

translations.literal: The ancients in teaching and drill required three years before completion — now troops have been used three years; of generals' talent who is worthy who is foolish, of attack-and-defense arts who gains who loses — years of defeat, yet those holding frontier posts do not know what plan.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient drill took three years; after three years of war we still do not know which frontier commanders are fit or which tactics work.

sentences.zh: 使更數年未罷兵，國用民力，何以克堪。

translations.literal: If several more years pass without ceasing troops, state revenue and popular strength — how can they be borne?
translations.idiomatic: If war drags on, how can treasury and people endure?

sentences.zh: 若因之以饑饉，加之以他寇，則安危之策，未知如何。

translations.literal: If on that famine is added, and other raiders are added — then policies for safety and danger, it is not known how.
translations.idiomatic: Add famine and other enemies, and no one knows what will keep the realm safe.

sentences.zh: 五也。

translations.literal: Fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth.

sentences.zh: 今言邊事者甚眾，朝廷或即奏可，或再詳究以聞，或付有司。

translations.literal: Now those who speak of border affairs are very many — the court sometimes immediately approves, sometimes examines again in detail and reports, or hands to the responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: Border memorials flood the court—some approved at once, some sent back for study, some delegated.

sentences.zh: 前條方行，後令即變，胥史有鈔錄之勞，官吏無商略之暇，邊防軍政，一無定制。

translations.literal: The prior article just executed, the later order immediately changes — clerks have the labor of copying, officials have no leisure for deliberation — frontier defense and military government entirely lack fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: New orders cancel old ones before clerks finish copying; frontier policy has no stable rules.

sentences.zh: 六也。

translations.literal: Sixth.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth.

sentences.zh: 夏竦、陳執中皆朝廷大臣，凡有邊事，當付之不疑。

translations.literal: Xia Song and Chen Zhizhong are both great ministers of the court — whenever there are border affairs, they should be entrusted without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers Xia Song and Chen Zhizhong should run border affairs with full trust.

sentences.zh: 今但主文書、守詔令，每有宣命，則翻錄行下；

translations.literal: Now they only manage documents and guard edicts — whenever there is an imperial order they copy and transmit downward;
translations.idiomatic: Instead they only file papers and relay edicts downward;

sentences.zh: 如諸處申稟，則令候朝旨。

translations.literal: if various places submit reports, they order them to await court instructions.
translations.idiomatic: local reports must wait for capital instructions.

sentences.zh: 如是，則何必以大臣主事？

translations.literal: If so, why must great ministers manage affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Why keep great ministers in charge at all?

sentences.zh: 七也。

translations.literal: Seventh.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh.

sentences.zh: 前河北用兵，減冗官以省費，今陝西日以增員，如制置青白鹽使副、招撫蕃部使臣十餘員，所占兵士千餘人，請給歲約萬緡。

translations.literal: Formerly in Hebei troops were used, redundant offices were cut to save expense — now in Shaanxi posts daily increase, such as commissioners deputy for green-white salt control, more than ten envoys to pacify tribal peoples — soldiers occupied over a thousand, requested stipends yearly about ten thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei had cut redundant posts to save money; Shaanxi multiplies salt and tribal commissioners costing ten thousand strings a year for a thousand idle troops.

sentences.zh: 復有都大提舉馬鋪器甲之類，諸州並募克敵、致勝、保捷、廣銳、宣毅等兵，久未曾團結訓練，但費軍廩，無益邊備。

translations.literal: Again there are overall chiefs for raising horse-forge arms and armor and the like; all prefectures recruit Ke-di, Zhi-sheng, Bao-jie, Guang-rui, Xuan-yi troops — long without regimentation and drill, only consuming army grain, no benefit to border defense.
translations.idiomatic: New armory chiefs and locally raised units drain rations without training or strengthening the border.

sentences.zh: 八也。

translations.literal: Eighth.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth.

sentences.zh: 今軍有手藝者，管兵之官，每一指揮，抽占三之一。

translations.literal: Now among troops with hand skills, the officer commanding troops in each command draws off one-third.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders skim a third of every skilled soldier from each unit.

sentences.zh: 如延州諸將不出，即有兵二萬，除五千守城之外，其餘止一萬五千。

translations.literal: If Yan Prefecture's various generals do not sortie, there are twenty thousand troops — aside from five thousand guarding the city, the rest are only fifteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanzhou twenty thousand men minus five thousand garrison leaves only fifteen thousand.

sentences.zh: 若有警急，三日內不能團集，況四十里外便是敵境，一有奔突，何以備之？

translations.literal: If there is sudden alarm, within three days they cannot be massed — moreover forty li outside is already enemy territory — once there is a rush attack, how prepare?
translations.idiomatic: They cannot muster in three days while the enemy sits forty li away—how meet a sudden raid?

sentences.zh: 九也。

translations.literal: Ninth.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth.

sentences.zh: 陝西教集鄉兵，共十餘萬人。

translations.literal: Shaanxi trained and gathered militia — altogether more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi militia exceed a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 市井無賴，名掛尺籍，心薄田夫，豈無奸盜雜於其中？

translations.literal: Market riffraff, names hung on the roster, hearts scorn farmers — surely there are rogues and thieves mixed among them?
translations.idiomatic: Market thugs on the rolls despise farmers—surely thieves hide among them.

sentences.zh: 苟無措置，他日為患不細。

translations.literal: If without arrangement, another day the harm will not be small.
translations.idiomatic: Without control they will become a grave menace.

sentences.zh: 十也。」

translations.literal: Tenth."
translations.idiomatic: Tenth."

sentences.zh: 既而復請面陳利害，不報。

translations.literal: Before long he again asked to state advantages and harms face to face — no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked to present his case in person and received no answer.

sentences.zh: 會元昊益熾，以兵圍河外。

translations.literal: It happened that Yuan Hao grew fiercer and with troops besieged the outer reaches of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao grew bolder and besieged the Yellow River frontier.

sentences.zh: 康德輿無守禦才，屬戶豪乜囉叛去，導夏人自後河川襲府州，兵至近道才覺，而蕃漢民被殺掠已眾。

translations.literal: Kang Deyu lacked talent for defense; dependent households' magnate Yeluo rebelled and left, guiding Xia people from rear river valleys to strike Fu Prefecture — troops reached the near road before they were noticed, and Fan and Han people killed and plundered were already many.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Deyu could not defend; tribal chief Yeluo guided Xia raiders up the rear river valleys into Fu before anyone noticed, slaughtering many.

sentences.zh: 攻城不能下，引兵屯琉璃堡，縱遊騎鈔麟、府間，二州閉壁不出。

translations.literal: They could not take the city by assault and led troops to encamp at Liuli Stockade, letting roaming cavalry raid between Lin and Fu — the two prefectures closed their walls and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Failing to storm the city, they camped at Liuli and raided between Lin and Fu while both towns shut their gates.

sentences.zh: 民乏飲，黃金一兩易水一杯。

translations.literal: The people lacked drink — one tael of yellow gold traded for one cup of water.
translations.idiomatic: Water sold for a tael of gold a cup.

sentences.zh: 時豐州已為夏人所破，麟、府勢孤，朝廷議棄河外守保德軍未果，徙亢為幷代都鈐轄、管勾麟府軍馬事。

translations.literal: At the time Feng Prefecture had already been broken by Xia people; Lin and Fu stood isolated — the court debated abandoning the outer river to hold Baode Army without result, and shifted Kang to overall military inspector of Bingdai and supervisor of Lin-Fu horse and foot affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Feng had fallen; Lin and Fu were isolated. The court hesitated to abandon the river bend but made Kang overall inspector of Bingdai and Lin-Fu forces.

sentences.zh: 單騎叩城，出所授敕示城上，門啟，既入，即縱民出采薪芻汲澗谷。

translations.literal: Alone on horseback he knocked at the city, showed the edict he carried to those on the wall — the gate opened; once inside he at once let the people go out to gather firewood, fodder, and draw from ravine streams.
translations.idiomatic: He rode alone to the gate, showed his edict, entered, and let the people forage for fuel and water.

sentences.zh: 然夏人猶時出鈔掠，亢以州東焦山有石炭穴，為築東勝堡；

translations.literal: Yet Xia people still sometimes came out to raid; Kang because east of the prefecture Jiao Mountain had coal pits, built Dongsheng Stockade;
translations.idiomatic: Xia raids continued; Kang built Dongsheng Stockade at Jiao Mountain's coal pits;

sentences.zh: 下城旁有蔬畦，為築金城堡；

translations.literal: below the city beside vegetable plots, built Jin Fort Stockade;
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fort Stockade by the city gardens;

sentences.zh: 州北沙坑有水泉，為築安定堡，置兵守之。

translations.literal: north of the prefecture sand pits had springs, built Anding Stockade, placed troops to guard.
translations.idiomatic: Anding Stockade at northern springs, each garrisoned.

sentences.zh: 募人獲於外，腰鐮與衛送者均得。

translations.literal: He recruited people to harvest outside — sickle at the waist, harvest split equally with escorts.
translations.idiomatic: Harvesters outside shared their sickle-cut gains equally with their guards.

sentences.zh: 其時禁兵皆敗北，無鬥志，乃募役兵敢戰者，夜伏隘道，邀擊夏人遊騎。

translations.literal: At that time palace troops had all been defeated north and had no fighting will — he then recruited corvée soldiers who dared fight, by night lay in narrow passes, intercepted and struck Xia roaming cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Demoralized palace troops were shamed when corvée volunteers ambushed Xia scouts at night.

sentences.zh: 比明，有持首級來獻者，亢以錦袍賜之，禁兵始慚奮曰：「我顧不若彼乎？」

translations.literal: When dawn came, some brought heads to present; Kang with brocade robes rewarded them — palace troops began ashamed and stirred and said: "Are we not as good as they?"
translations.idiomatic: At dawn head-bearers won brocade robes; the palace troops asked, "Are we worse than they?"

sentences.zh: 又縱使飲博，方窘乏幸利，咸願一戰。

translations.literal: Again he let them drink and gamble — in dire want coveting profit, all wished one battle.
translations.idiomatic: He let them drink and gamble until broke men begged for a fight.

sentences.zh: 亢知可用，始謀擊琉璃堡，使諜伏敵砦旁草中，見老羌方炙羊髀占吉凶，驚曰：「明當有急兵，且趣避之。」

translations.literal: Kang knew they could be used and first planned to strike Liuli Stockade, sending spies to lie in grass beside the enemy stockade — seeing old Qiang roasting sheep thigh to divine fortune and disaster, startled said: "Tomorrow there will be urgent troops — hurry avoid."
translations.idiomatic: Planning to hit Liuli, spies heard old Qiang divining over mutton: "Enemy tomorrow—flee."

sentences.zh: 皆笑曰：「漢兒皆藏頭膝間，何敢！」

translations.literal: All laughed and said: "Han lads all hide head between knees — how dare!"
translations.idiomatic: They laughed: "Song men hide their heads—how would they dare?"

sentences.zh: 亢知無備，夜引兵襲擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Kang knew they were unprepared; by night led troops in surprise attack and greatly broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Kang struck by night and routed them.

sentences.zh: 夏人棄堡去，乃築宣威砦於步駝溝捍寇路。

translations.literal: Xia people abandoned the stockade and left; he then built Xuanwei Stockade at Butuo Gully to block the bandit road.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia abandoned Liuli; Kang built Xuanwei Stockade on the raider path.

sentences.zh: 時麟州饋路猶未通，敕亢自護賞物送麟州。

translations.literal: At that time Lin Prefecture's supply road was still not open — the emperor ordered Kang himself to escort reward goods to Lin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's supply line was still cut; Kang was ordered to escort provisions there himself.

sentences.zh: 敵既不得鈔，遂以兵數萬趨柏子砦來邀。

translations.literal: The enemy, unable to raid, then with tens of thousands of troops hurried to Bozi Stockade to intercept.
translations.idiomatic: Denied raids, the enemy massed tens of thousands to ambush him at Bozi Stockade.

sentences.zh: 亢所將才三千人，亢激怒之曰：「若等已陷死地，前鬥則生，不然，為賊所屠無餘也。」

translations.literal: Those Kang led were only three thousand; Kang angrily roused them saying: "You are already in dead ground — fight forward then live, otherwise the bandits will butcher you without remainder."
translations.idiomatic: With only three thousand men he shouted: "Fight or die—no mercy if you flee."

sentences.zh: 士皆感厲。

translations.literal: The soldiers all were moved and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: The men roared back.

sentences.zh: 會天大風，順風擊之，斬首六百餘級，相蹂踐赴崖谷死者不可勝計，奪馬千餘匹。

translations.literal: It happened that heaven sent great wind; striking with the wind they took more than six hundred heads — those trampled and plunging into cliffs and valleys dead could not be counted; they seized more than a thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: A gale favored them; six hundred heads fell and countless men and horses plunged off cliffs; a thousand horses were captured.

sentences.zh: 乃修建寧砦。

translations.literal: Thereupon he built and repaired Ning Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He then built Ning Stockade.

sentences.zh: 夏人數出爭，遂戰於兔毛川。

translations.literal: Xia people several times came out to contend; they fought at Tumao River.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia fought him repeatedly at Tumaomao River.

sentences.zh: 亢自抗以大陣，而使驍將張岊伏短兵強弩數千於山後。

translations.literal: Kang himself opposed with the great array, while making fierce general Zhang Bian hide short weapons and powerful crossbows numbering several thousand behind the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Kang held the main line while Zhang Bian hid thousands of crossbowmen behind the hill.

sentences.zh: 亢以萬勝軍皆京師新募市井無賴子弟，罷軟不能戰，敵目曰「東軍」，素易之，而怯虎翼軍勇悍。

translations.literal: Kang because the Wansheng Army were all newly recruited market riffraff from the capital, soft and unable to fight — the enemy called them "Eastern Army" and always despised them, yet feared the Tiger Wing Army's fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy despised the soft "Eastern Army" recruits but feared the Tiger Wing veterans.

sentences.zh: 亢陰易其旗以誤敵，敵果趣 「東軍」，而值虎翼卒，搏戰良久，伏發，敵大潰，斬首二千級。

translations.literal: Kang secretly exchanged their banners to mislead the enemy — the enemy indeed rushed the "Eastern Army" but met Tiger Wing soldiers; they fought long and the ambush released — the enemy greatly routed, two thousand heads cut.
translations.idiomatic: Kang swapped banners; the enemy charged the "Eastern Army" and met Tiger Wings; the ambush broke them—two thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 不逾月，築清塞、百勝、中候、建寧、鎮川五堡，麟、府之路始通。

translations.literal: Within a month he built Qingse, Baisheng, Zhonghou, Jianning, and Zhenchuan five stockades — the Lin-Fu road was first opened.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month five stockades opened the Lin-Fu road.

sentences.zh: 亢復奏：「今所通特一徑爾，請更增並邊諸柵以相維持，則可以廣田牧，壯河外之勢。」

translations.literal: Kang again memorialized: "What is now open is only one path — please further add stockades along the border to mutually support, then pasture and fields can be broadened and outer-river power strengthened."
translations.idiomatic: He asked for more border stockades to widen pasture and strengthen the river bend.

sentences.zh: 議未下，會契丹欲渝盟，領果州團練使、知瀛州。

translations.literal: Deliberation had not concluded when the Khitan wished to break the alliance — he was made regimental commander of Guo Prefecture and prefect of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Before the court decided, the Khitan threatened the treaty and he was sent to Ying as Guo regimental commander.

sentences.zh: 葛懷敏敗，遷四方館使、涇原路經略安撫招討使、知渭州，亢聞詔即行，及至，敵已去。

translations.literal: When Ge Huaimin was defeated, he was shifted to envoy of the Four Directions Hall, Jingyuan frontier pacification and punitive commissioner, prefect of Wei — Kang heard the edict and at once departed; when he arrived the enemy had already left.
translations.idiomatic: After Ge Huaimin's defeat he was rushed to Jingyuan as pacification commissioner but arrived after the enemy left.

sentences.zh: 鄭戩統四路，亢與議不合，遷引進使，徙幷代副都總管。

translations.literal: Zheng Xian commanded four circuits; Kang disagreed with him in counsel and was shifted to promotion commissioner, moved to Bingdai deputy overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: He clashed with four-circuit commander Zheng Xian and was moved to Bingdai deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 御史梁堅劾亢出庫銀給牙吏往成都市易，以利自入，奪引進使，為本路鈐轄。

translations.literal: Censor Liang Jian impeached Kang for taking treasury silver to give clerks to go to Chengdu for market trade, profiting for himself — he was stripped of promotion commissioner and made military inspector of the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liang Jian accused him of using treasury silver for Chengdu trade for personal gain and demoted him to circuit inspector.

sentences.zh: 及夏人與契丹戰河外，復引進使、副都總管，知代州兼河東沿邊安撫事。

translations.literal: When Xia people and Khitan fought in the outer river, he again became promotion commissioner and deputy overall commander, prefect of Dai Prefecture concurrently Hebei along-the-border pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia and Khitan fought on the frontier he again became promotion commissioner and Dai prefect with Hebei border duties.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹宣撫河東，復奏亢前所增廣堡砦，宜使就總其事。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan as pacification commissioner of Hedong again memorialized that the stockades Kang had earlier added should let him overall supervise the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan urged that Kang finish the stockades he had planned.

sentences.zh: 詔既下，明鎬以為不可，屢牒止之。

translations.literal: The edict had descended when Ming Hao held it impossible and repeatedly sent documents to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Hao repeatedly ordered him to stop building.

sentences.zh: 亢曰：「受詔置堡砦，豈可得經略牒而止耶？

translations.literal: Kang said: "Receiving orders to set stockades — how can one stop because of a frontier commissioner's document?
translations.idiomatic: Kang said, "Imperial orders to build stockades are not canceled by a frontier memo.

sentences.zh: 坐違節度，死所甘心，堡砦必為也。」

translations.literal: For violating command, death is willingly accepted — the stockades will be built.
translations.idiomatic: I accept death for disobedience—the stockades will stand."

sentences.zh: 每得牒，置案上，督役愈急。

translations.literal: Each time he received a document he placed it on the desk and supervised labor all the more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Each stop-order went on his desk while work sped up.

sentences.zh: 及堡成，乃發封自劾，朝廷置不問。

translations.literal: When the stockades were complete he then opened the seal and impeached himself — the court set the matter aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When the forts were done he impeached himself; the court ignored it.

sentences.zh: 蕃漢歸者數千戶，歲減戍兵萬人，河外遂為幷、汾屏蔽。

translations.literal: Fan and Han returning numbered several thousand households; yearly garrison troops were reduced ten thousand — the outer river thus became a screen for Bing and Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of families returned; ten thousand garrison troops were cut; the river bend shielded Bing and Fen.

sentences.zh: 復知瀛州，因言：「州小而人眾，緩急無所容，若廣東南關，則民居皆在城中。」

translations.literal: Again made prefect of Ying and thereupon said: "The prefecture is small yet people numerous — in urgency there is nowhere to hold; if the southeast pass is broadened, then civilian dwellings are all within the city."
translations.idiomatic: As Ying prefect he urged widening the southeast gate so the crowded town could shelter everyone in a siege.

sentences.zh: 夏竦前在陝西，惡亢不附己，特沮其役，然卒城之。

translations.literal: Xia Song before in Shaanxi hated Kang for not attaching to him and especially obstructed the project — yet in the end the wall was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song, who disliked him, tried to block the wall but it was finished anyway.

sentences.zh: 加領眉州防禦使，復為涇原路總管、知渭州。

translations.literal: Added concurrently defender of Meizhou, again Jingyuan overall commander and Wei prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He again commanded Jingyuan and served as Meizhou defender.

sentences.zh: 會給郊賞，州庫物良而估賤，三司所給物下而估高，亢命均其直，以便軍人。

translations.literal: It happened that suburban rewards were issued — prefectural store goods were good yet appraised low, while the three departments' goods were inferior yet appraised high; Kang ordered equalize the values to convenience the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He equalized shoddy central goods and good local goods in suburban rewards so soldiers were not cheated.

sentences.zh: 轉運使奏亢擅減三司所估。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner memorialized that Kang on his own authority reduced the three departments' appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner accused him of cutting central appraisals.

sentences.zh: 會竦為樞密使，奪防禦使，降知磁州。

translations.literal: It happened that Song was Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner — he stripped defender and demoted to prefect of Ci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song as military commissioner demoted him to Ci prefect.

sentences.zh: 御史宋禧繼言亢嘗以庫銀市易，復奪引進使，為右領衛大將軍、知壽州。

translations.literal: Censor Song Xi again said Kang once used treasury silver in trade — again stripped promotion commissioner, made right leader of the imperial guard great general and prefect of Shou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Song Xi renewed the silver charge and made him a guard general at Shou.

sentences.zh: 後陝西轉運使言亢所易庫銀非自入者，改將作監、知和州。

translations.literal: Later Shaanxi transport commissioner said the treasury silver Kang traded was not for self-enrichment — changed to director of palace construction and prefect of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later inquiry cleared the silver trade; he became palace construction director at He.

sentences.zh: 坐失舉，徙筠州。

translations.literal: Punished for faulty recommendation, shifted to Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A bad recommendation sent him to Yun.

sentences.zh: 久之，復為引進使、果州團練使，又復眉州防禦使、真定府路副都總管。

translations.literal: Before long again promotion commissioner and Guo regimental commander, again Meizhou defender and Zhending circuit deputy overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: He soon regained promotion commissioner rank and Zhending deputy command.

sentences.zh: 遷客省使，以足疾知衛州，徙懷州。

translations.literal: Shifted to guest-relations commissioner; because of foot ailment made prefect of Wei Prefecture, shifted to Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Foot trouble made him Wei then Huai prefect.

sentences.zh: 坐與鄰郡守議河事，會境上經夕而還，降曹州鈐轄。

translations.literal: Punished for with a neighboring prefecture's administrator discussing river affairs, crossing the border overnight and returning — demoted to Cao Prefecture military inspector.
translations.idiomatic: A night crossing into a neighbor's territory to discuss river works cost him his post to Cao inspector.

sentences.zh: 改河陽總管，以疾辭，為秘書監。

translations.literal: Changed to Heyang overall commander; citing illness resigned, made secretary director.
translations.idiomatic: He became Heyang commander, then secretary director on illness.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復客省使、眉州防禦使、徐州總管，卒。

translations.literal: Before long again guest-relations commissioner, Meizhou defender, Xuzhou overall commander — died.
translations.idiomatic: He briefly returned as Xuzhou commander and died.

sentences.zh: 亢好施輕財，凡燕犒饋遺，類皆過厚，至遣人貿易助其費，猶不足。

translations.literal: Kang liked giving and treated wealth lightly — all banquets, rewards, and gifts were generally excessive; he even sent men to trade to supplement the cost, still insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Kang gave lavishly, even trading to pay for feasts and gifts.

sentences.zh: 以此人樂為之用。

translations.literal: Because of this men delighted to be used by him.
translations.idiomatic: Men gladly served such a generous commander.

sentences.zh: 同學生為吏部，亢憐其老，薦為縣令。

translations.literal: A fellow student became an official in the Ministry of Personnel; Kang pitied his age and recommended him as county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended an aged classmate from the Ministry of Personnel as county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 後既為所累，出筠州，還，所薦者復求濟，亢又贈金帛，終不以屑意。

translations.literal: Later already harmed by him, exiled to Yun Prefecture — on return the one he had recommended again sought aid; Kang again gave gold and silk, to the end not minding it.
translations.idiomatic: That man later ruined him; after exile the same man begged again and Kang still gave gold without resentment.

sentences.zh: 馭軍嚴明，所至有風跡，民圖像祠之。

translations.literal: He governed troops with strict clarity; wherever he went there were traces of style — the people painted images and sacrificed to him.
translations.idiomatic: His strict command left a mark; people enshrined his portrait.

sentences.zh: 兄 奎

translations.literal: Elder brother Kui
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Kui

sentences.zh: 奎，字仲野，先亢中進士。

translations.literal: Kui, courtesy name Zhongye, before Kang passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Kui, style name Zhongye, took the jinshi before his brother.

sentences.zh: 歷幷、秀州推官，監衢州酒。

translations.literal: He passed through investigating officer of Bing and Xiu prefectures, supervised Qu Prefecture wine.
translations.idiomatic: He served as investigator in Bing and Xiu and as Qu wine supervisor.

sentences.zh: 徐生者毆人至死，繫婺州獄，再問輒言冤。

translations.literal: A man Xu beat a man to death, was bound in Wu Prefecture prison — questioned again he always said he was wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, held for beating a man to death in Wu, insisted he was innocent.

sentences.zh: 轉運使命奎復治。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner ordered Kui to retry the case.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner sent Kui to retry the case.

sentences.zh: 奎視囚籍印窾偽，深探之，乃獄吏竄易，卒釋徐生，抵吏罪，眾驚伏。

translations.literal: Kui viewed the prisoner register — seal and mortise were forged; probing deeply, it was the jail clerk who had altered it — in the end Xu was released, the clerk punished for crime; the crowd was astonished and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Kui found forged seals on the register, exposed the jail clerk, freed Xu, and awed the crowd.

sentences.zh: 同時薦者三十九人，改大理寺丞，知合淝縣，徙南充縣。

translations.literal: At the same time thirty-nine were recommended; changed to director of the Court of Judicial Review, made prefect of Hefei County, shifted to Nanchong County.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended with thirty-nine others, he became a judicial director and magistrate of Hefei and Nanchong.

sentences.zh: 以殿中丞通判瀘州，罷歸。

translations.literal: As palace inside censor he transited Luzhou and was dismissed to return.
translations.idiomatic: As palace censor he served at Luzhou and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 會秦州鹽課虧緡錢數十萬，事連十一州。

translations.literal: It happened that Qin Prefecture salt monopoly revenue was short tens of thousands of strings — the affair implicated eleven prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: A Qin salt deficit implicated eleven prefectures.

sentences.zh: 詔奎往按，還奏三司發鈔稽緩，非諸州罪。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Kui to go investigate; on return he memorialized that the three departments' issuing of notes was slow — not the prefectures' crime.
translations.idiomatic: Kui found the three departments slow to issue notes, not local guilt.

sentences.zh: 因言：「鹽法所以足軍費，非仁政所宜行。

translations.literal: Thereupon he said: "The salt law is to fill army expenses — it is not what benevolent government should practice.
translations.idiomatic: He argued the salt monopoly funds the army but is not benevolent policy.

sentences.zh: 若不得已，令商人轉貿流通，獨關市收其徵，上下皆利。

translations.literal: If there is no help for it, let merchants turn trade in circulation — only at passes and markets collect their levies — above and below all profit.
translations.idiomatic: Better let merchants circulate salt and tax only at passes, benefiting all.

sentences.zh: 孰與設重禁壅閼之為民病？」

translations.literal: How compare with setting heavy prohibitions and choking blockage to make sickness for the people?"
translations.idiomatic: How is that worse than choking trade with harsh bans?

sentences.zh: 於是悉除所負。

translations.literal: Thereupon all owed amounts were entirely remitted.
translations.idiomatic: All debts were forgiven.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知江州，徙楚州，遷太常博士，召為殿中侍御史、知滑州，徙邢州。

translations.literal: Before long made prefect of Jiang Prefecture, shifted to Chu Prefecture, promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, summoned as palace remonstrance censor and prefect of Hua Prefecture, shifted to Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became Jiang and Chu prefect, erudite of imperial sacrifices, remonstrance censor, and prefect of Hua and Xing.

sentences.zh: 母病，輒割股肉和藥以進，母遂愈。

translations.literal: When his mother was ill, he at once cut flesh from his thigh and mixed it in medicine to present — his mother then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill he cut thigh flesh for medicine and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 其後母卒，廬於墓，自負土植松柏。

translations.literal: Afterward when his mother died, he built a hut at the tomb and himself carried earth and planted pines and cypresses.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died he lived at her tomb, carrying earth and planting pines himself.

sentences.zh: 服終，授度支判官，出為京東轉運使，以侍御史為河東轉運使，進刑部員外郎、知御史雜事。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed revenue-section judge, went out as Hedong transport commissioner, with remonstrance censor served as Hedong transport commissioner, advanced to vice director of the Ministry of Justice and supervisor of assorted censorial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he rose through revenue and transport posts to vice minister of justice and censorial supervisor.

sentences.zh: 安撫京東，募民充軍凡十二萬，奏州縣吏能否數十人。

translations.literal: Pacifying Hedong, he recruited civilians as soldiers altogether a hundred twenty thousand, memorialized the ability of prefecture and county clerks numbering several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying Hedong he raised a hundred twenty thousand militia and rated dozens of local officials.

sentences.zh: 還為戶部副使。

translations.literal: On return he became vice commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as vice revenue commissioner.

sentences.zh: 及分陝西為四路，擢天章閣待制、環慶路經略安撫招討使、知慶州，以父名餘慶辭，不許。

translations.literal: When Shaanxi was divided into four circuits, he was promoted to Hanlin associate of the Tianzhang Pavilion, Huanqing frontier pacification and punitive commissioner, prefect of Qing Prefecture — because his father's name was Yuqing he declined, not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi split into four circuits he became Huanqing pacification commissioner and Qing prefect; he declined the post because his father's name was Yuqing but was overruled.

sentences.zh: 歷陝西都轉運使、知永興軍、河東都轉運使，加龍圖閣直學士，知澶、青、徐、揚等州，再遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He passed through Shaanxi overall transport commissioner, prefect of Yongxing Army, Hedong overall transport commissioner, added direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, made prefect of Chan, Qing, Xu, Yang and other prefectures, again promoted to director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Shaanxi and Hedong transport commissioner, Yongxing prefect, and prefect of several eastern circuits, rising to personnel director.

sentences.zh: 時李宥知江寧府，府廨盡焚。

translations.literal: At the time Li You was prefect of Jiangning — the government offices were entirely burned.
translations.idiomatic: Li You's Jiangning government compound had burned to the ground.

sentences.zh: 諫官言金陵始封之地，守臣視火不謹，宜擇才臣繕治之。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials said Jinling was the land of the first enfeoffment — the guardian minister viewed fire carelessly and a talented minister should be chosen to repair.
translations.idiomatic: Censors said Jinling, the dynasty's first capital, needed a capable rebuild after the fire.

sentences.zh: 遷右諫議大夫、知江寧府。

translations.literal: He was shifted to right remonstrance grandee and made prefect of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was made right remonstrance grandee and Jiangning prefect.

sentences.zh: 奎簡材料工，一循舊制，不逾時復完。

translations.literal: Kui selected materials and craftsmen, entirely following old regulations — without exceeding the time it was again complete.
translations.idiomatic: Kui rebuilt on the old plan with chosen craftsmen, finishing on schedule.

sentences.zh: 還，判吏部流內銓，徙審官院、知河南府。

translations.literal: On return he judged the Ministry of Personnel's flowing-within roster, shifted to the Court of Review and made prefect of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he ran personnel rosters, then became Henan prefect.

sentences.zh: 河南宮闕歲久頗摧圮，奎大加興葺。

translations.literal: Henan's palaces and gates, years long, were quite ruined — Kui greatly undertook repair.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Henan's long-ruined palaces and gates.

sentences.zh: 又按唐街陌，分榜諸坊。

translations.literal: Again he followed Tang streets and lanes, dividing and posting the wards.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Tang street grids and posted ward signs.

sentences.zh: 初，全義守洛四十年，洛人德之，有生祠。

translations.literal: At first Quanyi guarded Luo forty years — Luoyang people cherished him and there was a living shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi had governed Luoyang forty years and the people had kept his living shrine.

sentences.zh: 及見奎偉儀觀，曰：「真齊王孫也。」

translations.literal: When they saw Kui's grand bearing and appearance they said: "Truly the Prince of Qi's descendant."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Kui's bearing they said, "Truly Quanyi's heir."

sentences.zh: 因復興齊王祠。

translations.literal: Thereupon they again raised the Prince of Qi shrine.
translations.idiomatic: They restored the Prince of Qi shrine.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以能政聞，遷給事中，歸朝。

translations.literal: After more than a year, because of able governance he was known, shifted to giving-the-throne attendant, returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: After a year his governance won praise and he returned to court as giving-the-throne attendant.

sentences.zh: 京東盜起，加樞密直學士、知鄆州，數月，捕諸盜，悉平。

translations.literal: Hedong bandits rose — added direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and made prefect of Yan Prefecture; within several months he captured the bandits and entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Hedong he became Yan prefect and cleared them within months.

sentences.zh: 奎治身有法度，風力精強，所至有治跡，吏不敢欺，第傷苛細。

translations.literal: Kui in governing himself had method and measure, spirit and strength refined and strong — wherever he went there were traces of good rule; clerks did not dare deceive — only he harmed by harsh minuteness.
translations.idiomatic: Kui ruled with discipline and force; clerks feared him, though some found him harsh.

sentences.zh: 亢豪放喜功名，不事小謹。

translations.literal: Kang was bold and unrestrained, delighting in achievement and fame, not troubling with small caution.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was bold, ambitious, and careless of small proprieties.

sentences.zh: 兄弟所為不同如此，然皆知名一時。

translations.literal: The brothers' conduct differed thus — yet both were famous in one generation.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers differed in character yet both won fame.

sentences.zh: 子燾，龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: Son Tao, direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tao became a Dragon Diagram academician.

sentences.zh: 劉文質

translations.literal: Liu Wenzhi
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenzhi

sentences.zh: 劉文質，字士彬，保州保塞人，簡穆皇后從孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Wenzhi, courtesy name Shibin, was a man of Baosai in Bao Prefecture — a collateral descendant of Empress Jianmu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenzhi, style name Shibin, of Baosai in Bao, was a kinsman of Empress Jianmu.

sentences.zh: 父審琦，虎牢關使，從討李重進戰死。

translations.literal: His father Shenqi was Tiger Cage Pass commissioner; following the campaign against Li Chongjin he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shenqi, Tiger Cage Pass commissioner, died fighting Li Chongjin.

sentences.zh: 文質幼從母入禁中，太宗授以左班殿直，遷西頭供奉官、寄班祗侯。

translations.literal: Wenzhi in youth followed his mother into the inner palace; Emperor Taizong appointed him left-class palace attendant, promoted to western-head palace attendant and duty usher.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in the palace, Taizong made him a left-class attendant and western-head usher.

sentences.zh: 帝頗親信之，數訪以外事。

translations.literal: The emperor quite trusted him and several times inquired of external affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong trusted him and often asked about outside affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂內侍竇神興曰：「文質，朕之近親，又忠謹，其賜白金百斤。」

translations.literal: Once he said to the inner attendant Dou Shenxing: "Wenzhi is Our close kin and again loyal and careful — give him a hundred jin of white gold."
translations.idiomatic: He told Dou Shenxing, "Wenzhi is kin and loyal—give him a hundred jin of silver."

sentences.zh: 出為兩浙走馬承受公事，擢西京左藏庫副使、岢嵐軍使，賜金帶、名馬。

translations.literal: He went out as Zhe-Liang traveling horse bearer of imperial orders, promoted to deputy commissioner of the Western Capital left treasury and Kailan Army commissioner, granted gold belt and famous horse.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Zhe-Liang as imperial courier, he became Kailan commissioner with gold belt and a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 徙知麟州，改麟府濁輪砦兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: Shifted to prefect of Lin Prefecture, changed to military inspector of Lin-Fu Zhuolun Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He became Lin prefect, then inspector of the Lin-Fu Zhuolun stockade.

sentences.zh: 擊蕃酋萬保移，走之。

translations.literal: He struck the tribal chief Wan Baoyi and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the tribal chief Wan Baoyi.

sentences.zh: 越河破契丹，拔黃太尉砦，殺獲萬計，賜錦袍、金帶。

translations.literal: Crossing the river he broke the Khitan, took Yellow Grand Marshal Stockade, killed and captured numbering in the tens of thousands — granted brocade robe and gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river, beat the Khitan, took Yellow Grand Marshal Stockade, and won tens of thousands of captives.

sentences.zh: 徙知慶州。

translations.literal: Shifted to prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became Qing prefect.

sentences.zh: 李繼遷入寇，文質將出兵，而官吏不敢發庫錢。

translations.literal: When Li Jiqian invaded, Wenzhi was about to lead troops out but officials and clerks did not dare release treasury money.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiqian invaded, officials would not release treasury funds for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 乃以私錢二百萬給軍，士皆感奮，遂大破賊。

translations.literal: He then with private money two million strings supplied the army — soldiers all were moved and stirred and thereupon greatly broke the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He paid two million strings from his own purse; the troops rallied and crushed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 徙涇州，充麟州、清遠軍都監，又破敵於枝子平。

translations.literal: Shifted to Jing Prefecture, filled Lin Prefecture and Qingyuan Army chief supervisor, again broke the enemy at Zhizi Plain.
translations.idiomatic: At Jing and as Lin-Qingyuan supervisor he again defeated the enemy at Zhizi Plain.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，清遠軍陷，坐逗撓奪官，雷州安置。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era Qingyuan Army fell — punished for delay and timidity, office stripped, settled at Lei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingyuan fell in Xianping he was demoted to Lei for delay.

sentences.zh: 久之，起為太子率府率、杭州駐泊都監。

translations.literal: Before long raised as crown prince's rate-fu rate and Hangzhou garrison chief supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made crown prince's rate and Hangzhou garrison chief.

sentences.zh: 封泰山，以內殿崇班為青、齊、淄、濰州巡檢。

translations.literal: At Mount Tai fengshan, with inner-palace honored class made inspector of Qing, Qi, Zi, and Wei prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: At the Mount Tai fengshan he inspected Qing, Qi, Zi, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 進禮賓副使、石隰緣邊同都巡檢使，徙秦州鈐轄。

translations.literal: Advanced to deputy commissioner of ritual guests and Shiyi border joint overall inspector, shifted to Qin Prefecture military inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He became ritual deputy commissioner and Shiyi border inspector, then Qin military inspector.

sentences.zh: 建小落門砦，親率士版築。

translations.literal: He built Xiaoluomen Stockade and personally led soldiers in rampart construction.
translations.idiomatic: He built Xiaoluomen Stockade and labored on the walls himself.

sentences.zh: 會李浚知秦州，因就賜白金五百兩。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Jun was prefect of Qin Prefecture — thereupon he was granted five hundred taels of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Jun governed Qin he received five hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 天禧中，知代州。

translations.literal: In the Tianxi era made prefect of Dai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxi he became Dai prefect.

sentences.zh: 先是，蕃部獲逃卒，給絹二匹、茶五斤，卒皆論死。

translations.literal: Before this, tribal departments capturing fugitive soldiers gave two bolts of silk and five jin of tea — the soldiers were all sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes had been paid silk and tea for captured deserters who were then executed.

sentences.zh: 時捕得百三十九人，文質取二十九人，以赦後論如法，餘悉配隸他州。

translations.literal: At the time one hundred thirty-nine were captured — Wenzhi took twenty-nine, after amnesty sentenced by law; the rest all were assigned to other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Of a hundred thirty-nine captives he executed twenty-nine after amnesty and assigned the rest elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 再遷內園使、知邠州，數從曹瑋出戰，築堡障。

translations.literal: Again promoted to inner-garden commissioner and prefect of Bin Prefecture — several times followed Cao Wei in battle, building stockade barriers.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted inner-garden commissioner and Bin prefect, he campaigned with Cao Wei and built fortifications.

sentences.zh: 復徙秦州鈐轄，領連州刺史，再知代州，卒。

translations.literal: Again shifted to Qin Prefecture military inspector, held Lian Prefecture prefect, again made prefect of Dai Prefecture — died.
translations.idiomatic: He again inspected Qin, held Lian, and died as Dai prefect.

sentences.zh: 厚賻其家，官子三人。

translations.literal: Generously compensated his family and enfeoffed three sons.
translations.idiomatic: The court richly compensated his family and enfeoffed three sons.

sentences.zh: 文質以簡穆親，又父死事，故前後賜予異諸將。

translations.literal: Wenzhi because of kinship to Jianmu and again his father's death in service, therefore before and after rewards differed from other generals.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kinship and his father's death in battle brought him unusual rewards.

sentences.zh: 真宗嘗問保塞之舊，文質上宣祖、太祖賜書五函。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong once asked about Baosai's old days — Wenzhi presented five cases of books bestowed by the Founding Ancestor and Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong asked about Baosai; Wenzhi presented five cases of founding emperors' letters.

sentences.zh: 仁宗亦以書賜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong also with books bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong too granted him imperial writings.

sentences.zh: 然性剛，喜評刺短長，於貴近無所避，故不大顯。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was rigid, delighting in criticizing others' faults — toward the noble and close he avoided nothing, therefore he was not greatly displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Rigid and outspoken, he criticized even the powerful and never rose highest.

sentences.zh: 子十六人，渙、滬皆知名。

translations.literal: Sons numbered sixteen — Huan and Hu were both famous.
translations.idiomatic: Of sixteen sons, Huan and Hu were best known.

sentences.zh: 子 渙

translations.literal: Son Huan
translations.idiomatic: His son Huan

sentences.zh: 渙，字仲章，以父任為將作監主簿，監并州倉。

translations.literal: Huan, courtesy name Zhongzhang, through his father's privilege was chief clerk of the Directorate of Palace Construction, supervised Bing Prefecture granary.
translations.idiomatic: Huan, style name Zhongzhang, entered as palace construction clerk and supervised Bing's granary.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，章獻太后臨朝久，渙謂天子年加長，上書請還政。

translations.literal: In the Tiansheng era, Empress Zhangxian long held court — Huan said the Son of Heaven's years were growing and submitted a memorial asking return of rule.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Zhangxian's regency Huan memorialized that the emperor was grown and should rule.

sentences.zh: 后震怒，將黥隸白州，呂夷簡、薛奎力諫得免。

translations.literal: The empress was shocked and angry, was about to tattoo and assign to Baizhou — Lü Yijian and Xue Kui strongly remonstrated and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The empress would have tattooed and exiled him; Lü Yijian and Xue Kui saved him.

sentences.zh: 仁宗親政，擢為右正言。

translations.literal: When Renzong personally governed, he was promoted to right rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took power Huan became right rectifier.

sentences.zh: 郭后廢，渙與孔道輔、范仲淹等伏闕爭之，皆罰金。

translations.literal: When Empress Guo was deposed, Huan with Kong Daofu, Fan Zhongyan and others prostrated at the palace gate to contend — all were fined gold.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Kong Daofu and Fan Zhongyan protesting Empress Guo's deposition and was fined.

sentences.zh: 會河東走馬承受奏，渙頃官并州，與營妓遊，黜通判磁州，尋知遼州。

translations.literal: It happened that Hedong traveling horse bearer memorialized — when Huan had lately been official at Bing Prefecture he associated with camp courtesans — demoted transit intendant of Ci Prefecture, soon made prefect of Liao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Accused of consorting with camp courtesans at Bing he was demoted to Ci intendant, then Liao prefect.

sentences.zh: 夏人叛，朝廷議遣使通河西唃氏，渙請行。

translations.literal: When Xia people rebelled, the court debated sending envoys to communicate with the Hexi Gus clan — Huan asked to go.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia rebelled Huan volunteered to treat with the Hexi Gus.

sentences.zh: 間道走青唐，諭以恩信。

translations.literal: By hidden path he went to Qingtang and instructed them with grace and trust.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Qingtang by secret route and won them with trust.

sentences.zh: 唃氏大集族帳，誓死捍邊，遣騎護出境，得其誓書與西州地圖以獻。

translations.literal: The Gus greatly gathered clan tents, swore to die defending the border, sent horse to escort beyond the border — obtained their oath document and Xizhou maps and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: The Gus swore to defend the border, escorted him out, and gave oath texts and maps of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 加直昭文館，遷陝西轉運使、由工部郎中知滄州，改吉州刺史，知保州。

translations.literal: Added direct academician of the Zhaowen Hall, shifted to Shaanxi transport commissioner, from director of the Ministry of Works made prefect of Cang Prefecture, changed to Ji Prefecture prefect, made prefect of Bao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became Zhaowen academician, Shaanxi transport commissioner, and prefect of Cang, Ji, and Bao.

sentences.zh: 州自戍卒叛後，兵益驕。

translations.literal: The prefecture since corvée soldiers rebelled, troops grew all the more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Since a corvée mutiny Bao's garrison had grown insolent.

sentences.zh: 渙至，虎翼軍謀舉城叛，民大恐。

translations.literal: When Huan arrived, the Tiger Wing Army plotted to rebel and seize the city — the people were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger Wing troops plotted to seize the city when Huan arrived.

sentences.zh: 渙單騎徐叩營，械首惡者歸，斬之，一軍帖服。

translations.literal: Huan alone on horseback slowly knocked at camp, shackled the chief villain and returned, beheaded him — the whole army submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He rode alone into camp, seized the ringleader, executed him, and the army submitted.

sentences.zh: 徙登州，益治刀魚船備海寇，寇不敢犯，詔嘉獎之。

translations.literal: Shifted to Deng Prefecture, further managed knife-fish boats against sea raiders — raiders did not dare violate; the emperor ordered praise and reward.
translations.idiomatic: At Deng he built patrol boats; sea raiders dared not approach and the emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 歷知邢、恩、冀、涇、澶五州。

translations.literal: He passed through prefect of Xing, En, Ji, Jing, and Chan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Xing, En, Ji, Jing, and Chan.

sentences.zh: 恩承賊蹂踐後，渙經理繕葺有敘，兵民犯法，一切用重典，威令大振。

translations.literal: En, having suffered bandit trampling, Huan managed repair in order — soldiers and civilians violating law, entirely used heavy statutes; prestige and orders greatly shook.
translations.idiomatic: Rebuilding ravaged En with harsh law he restored order and awe.

sentences.zh: 治平中，河北地震，民乏粟，率賤賣耕牛以苟朝夕。

translations.literal: In the Zhiping era Hebei earthquake — the people lacked grain and mostly sold plow oxen cheap to scrape morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: After a Hebei earthquake farmers sold oxen cheap to buy food.

sentences.zh: 渙在澶，盡發公錢買之。

translations.literal: Huan at Chan entirely released public money to buy them.
translations.idiomatic: At Chan Huan used public funds to buy the oxen.

sentences.zh: 明年，民無牛耕，價增十倍，渙復出所市牛，以元直與民，澶民賴不失業。

translations.literal: The next year the people had no oxen to plow — price increased tenfold; Huan again released the oxen he had bought, at original value to the people — Chan people relied on this not to lose livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he sold the oxen back at cost so Chan farmers could plow.

sentences.zh: 歷秦鳳、涇原、真定、定州路總管，四遷至鎮寧軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: He passed through overall commander of Qinfeng, Jingyuan, Zhending, and Dingzhou circuits — four promotions to military commissioner and observation remnant of Zhenning Army.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded four circuits and rose to Zhenning military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，還，為工部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: In the Xining era he returned and as minister of the Ministry of Works retired.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining he retired as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 渙有才略，尚氣不羈，臨事無所避，然銳於進取。

translations.literal: Huan had talent and stratagem, valued spirit and was unrestrained — facing affairs he avoided nothing, yet he was sharp in advancing and seizing.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and bold, he shirked nothing yet hungered for advancement.

sentences.zh: 方升拓洮、岷，討安南，渙既老，猶露章請自效，不報。

translations.literal: When expanding Tuo and Min and attacking Annan, Huan though old still exposed memorials asking to serve in person — no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Though eighty he volunteered for the Tuo-Min and Annan campaigns and was ignored.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: He died, age eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 子 滬

translations.literal: Son Hu
translations.idiomatic: His son Hu

sentences.zh: 滬，字子浚，頗知書傳，深沉寡言，有知略。

translations.literal: Hu, courtesy name Zijun, quite knew books and classics, deep and silent with few words, had knowledge and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Hu, style name Zijun, was learned, quiet, and shrewd.

sentences.zh: 以蔭補三班奉職，累遷右侍禁。

translations.literal: By privilege supplemented third-class attendant, promoted in succession to right palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: By privilege he rose to right palace guard.

sentences.zh: 康定中，為渭州瓦亭砦監押，權靜邊砦，擊破黨留等族，斬一驍將，獲馬牛橐駝萬計。

translations.literal: In the Kangding era he was Wating Stockade supervisor of Wei Prefecture, acting Jingbian Stockade — broke the Dangliu and other clans, beheaded one fierce general, obtained horses, cattle, and camels numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At Wating he smashed the Dangliu clans, killed a fierce chief, and took vast herds.

sentences.zh: 時任福敗，邊城晝閉，居民畜產多為賊所掠，滬獨開門納之。

translations.literal: At the time Ren Fu was defeated — border cities closed by day; civilian livestock was mostly plundered by bandits — Hu alone opened gates to admit them.
translations.idiomatic: After Ren Fu's defeat he alone opened his gates to refugees while others were looted.

sentences.zh: 遷左侍禁，韓琦、范仲淹薦授閤門祗候。

translations.literal: Promoted left palace guard; Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan recommended appointing palace gate usher.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan made him a palace gate usher.

sentences.zh: 又破穆寧生氐。

translations.literal: Again broke the Muning Sheng Di.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated the Muning Sheng Di.

sentences.zh: 西南去略陽二百里，中有城曰水洛，川平土沃，又有水輪、銀、銅之利，環城數萬帳，漢民之逋逃者歸之，教其百工商賈，自成完國。

translations.literal: Southwest two hundred li from Lueyang there is a city called Shuiluo — the river plain soil fertile, again having water wheels and silver and copper profits; surrounding the city tens of thousands of tents — Han people who fled and returned to them taught their hundred crafts and merchants, themselves completing a state.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred li southwest lay Shuiluo, fertile and rich in metals, a mini-state of fugitive Han teaching crafts to tens of thousands of tents.

sentences.zh: 曹瑋在秦州，嘗經營不能得。

translations.literal: Cao Wei at Qin Prefecture once managed but could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wei had failed to take Shuiluo from Qin.

sentences.zh: 滬進城章川，收善田數百頃，以益屯兵，密使人說城主鐸廝那令內附。

translations.literal: Hu advanced to Zhangchuan city, collected good fields several hundred qing to augment garrison troops, secretly sent men to persuade the city lord Tiesina to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: Hu seized farmland near Zhangchuan and secretly won lord Tiesina's submission.

sentences.zh: 會鄭戩行邊，滬遂召鐸廝那及其酋屬來獻結公、水洛、路羅甘地，願為屬戶。
