translations.literal: It happened that Zheng Xian toured the border — Hu then summoned Tiesina and his chieftains to come present Jiegong, Shuiluo, and Luoluo Gan lands, wishing to become dependent households.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Xian toured the border Tiesina surrendered Jiegong, Shuiluo, and Luoluo Gan.

sentences.zh: 戩即令滬將兵往受地。

translations.literal: Xian then ordered Hu to lead troops to go receive the land.
translations.idiomatic: Xian ordered Hu to occupy the surrendered lands.

sentences.zh: 既至而氐情中變，聚兵數萬合圍，夜縱火呼嘯，期盡殺官軍。

translations.literal: Having arrived, Di sentiment midway changed — they gathered troops tens of thousands combined siege, by night set fire shouting, set on utterly killing the government army.
translations.idiomatic: The Di rebelled, besieging his thousand men by night with tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 滬兵才千人，前後數百里無援，滬堅臥，因令晨炊緩食，坐胡床指揮進退，一戰氐潰，追奔至石門，酋皆稽顙請服。

translations.literal: Hu's troops were only a thousand — before and behind several hundred li without aid; Hu lay firm, then ordered morning cooking slow eating, sat on a folding chair directing advance and retreat — one battle Di routed, pursued to Shimen — chiefs all knocked forehead requesting submission.
translations.idiomatic: With a thousand men and no relief Hu ate slowly from a camp chair, routed the Di, and chased them to Shimen.

sentences.zh: 因盡驅其眾隸麾下，以通秦、渭之路。

translations.literal: Thereupon he entirely drove their masses to attach under his banner — opening the road connecting Qin and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He enrolled the tribes and opened the Qin-Wei road.

sentences.zh: 又敗臨洮氐於城下。

translations.literal: Again defeated Lintao Di below the city.
translations.idiomatic: He beat the Lintao Di below the walls.

sentences.zh: 遷內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Promoted inner-palace honored class.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to inner-palace honored class.

sentences.zh: 戩以三將兵遣董士廉助築城，功未半，會戩罷四路招討使，而涇原路尹洙以為不便，令罷築，且召滬，不聽，日增版趣役。

translations.literal: Xian with three generals sent Dong Shilian to help build the city — work not half done, it happened Xian was dismissed four-circuit punitive commissioner, while Jingyuan Circuit's Yin Zhu held it inconvenient, ordered stop building and moreover summon Hu — not listening, daily increased boards urging labor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Zhu canceled the fort and recalled Hu, Hu kept building faster.

sentences.zh: 洙怒，使狄青械滬、士廉下獄。

translations.literal: Zhu was angry and made Di Qing shackle Hu and Shilian and put them in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhu had Di Qing arrest Hu and Dong Shilian.

sentences.zh: 氐眾驚，收積聚、殺吏民為亂，朝廷遣魚周詢、程戡往視，氐眾詣周詢，請以牛羊及丁壯助工役，復以滬權水洛城砦主。

translations.literal: Di masses were alarmed, gathered stores, killed officials and people in disorder — the court sent Yu Zhouxun and Cheng Kan to inspect; Di masses went to Zhouxun, asked to use cattle and sheep and adult males to help labor, again made Hu acting Shuiluo city stockade chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Di rioted until Yu Zhouxun restored Hu as Shuiluo chief with tribal labor.

sentences.zh: 城成，終以違本路安撫使節制，黜一官，為鎮戎軍西路都巡檢。

translations.literal: When the city was complete, in the end because of violating this circuit pacification commissioner's command, one office was demoted — made western-route overall inspector of Zhenrong Army.
translations.idiomatic: The city finished, he lost one rank for disobeying the pacification commissioner and became Zhenrong western inspector.

sentences.zh: 復內殿崇班，瘍發首，卒。

translations.literal: Again inner-palace honored class — carbuncle broke at the head — died.
translations.idiomatic: Restored to honored class, he died of a head abscess.

sentences.zh: 弟淵將以其柩東歸，居人遮道號泣請留，葬水洛，立祠城隅，歲時祀之。

translations.literal: Younger brother Yuan was about to take the coffin east to return home — residents blocked the road weeping and asking he stay; buried at Shuiluo, established a shrine at the city corner, yearly seasons sacrificed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Yuan tried to take the body home but the people wept and begged to keep him; they buried Hu at Shuiluo and built a shrine.

sentences.zh: 經略司言，得熟戶蕃官牛裝等狀，願得滬子弟主其城。

translations.literal: The frontier commission said they obtained statements from registered-household tribal officials Niu Zhuang and others, wishing to have Hu's sons and younger brothers govern the city.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal officers petitioned for Hu's kin to command Shuiluo.

sentences.zh: 乃命其弟淳為水洛城兵馬監押，城中有碑記滬事。

translations.literal: Thereupon ordered his younger brother Chun as Shuiluo city horse-and-foot supervisor — in the city there is a stele recording Hu's deeds.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Chun became Shuiluo garrison chief; a stele in the city records Hu's deeds.

sentences.zh: 趙滋，字子深，開封人。

translations.literal: Zhao Zi, courtesy name Zishen, was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zi, style name Zishen, was from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父士隆，天聖中，以閤門祗候為邠寧環慶路都監，戰沒。

translations.literal: His father Shilong in the Tiansheng era, as palace gate usher, was Binning-Huanqing overall supervisor — died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shilong died fighting as Binning-Huanqing supervisor in Tiansheng.

sentences.zh: 錄滋三班奉職。

translations.literal: Zi was recorded as third-class attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zi entered service as third-class attendant by his father's merit.

sentences.zh: 滋少果敢任氣，有智略。

translations.literal: Zi in youth was bold and daring, spirited — had wisdom and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Young Zi was bold, spirited, and shrewd.

sentences.zh: 康定初，以右侍禁選捕京西叛卒有功，遷左侍禁，後為涇原儀渭、鎮戎軍都巡檢。

translations.literal: At the start of Kangding, as right palace guard selected to capture western-capital rebels with achievement — promoted left palace guard, later became Jingyuan Yi-Wei and Zhenrong Army overall inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangding he captured western rebels and became Jingyuan and Zhenrong inspector.

sentences.zh: 會渭州得勝砦主姚貴殺監押崔絢，劫宣武神騎卒千餘人叛，攻羊牧隆城。

translations.literal: It happened at Wei Prefecture Desheng Stockade chief Yao Gui killed supervisor Cui Xuan, seized more than a thousand Xuanwu divine cavalry soldiers and rebelled, attacked Yangmulong city.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Gui killed his supervisor, seized a thousand Xuanwu cavalry, and attacked Yangmulong.

sentences.zh: 滋馳至，諭降八百餘人，貴窮，走出砦。

translations.literal: Zi galloped there, instructed and persuaded more than eight hundred to surrender — Gui exhausted, fled out of the stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Zi rushed in and persuaded eight hundred to surrender; Yao Gui fled.

sentences.zh: 招討使令滋給賜降卒及遷補將吏，滋以為如是是誘其為亂，藏其牒不用，還，為招討使所怒，故賞弗行。

translations.literal: The punitive commissioner ordered Zi to give rewards to surrendered soldiers and transfer and supplement officers — Zi held that thus was to entice them to rebel, hid the document and did not use it; on return the punitive commissioner was angry, therefore rewards were not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Zi refused to reward the mutineers lest it encourage rebellion and lost his own reward.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹、韓琦經略陝西，舉滋可將領，得閤門祗候，為鎮戎軍西路都巡檢。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan and Han Qi as frontier commissioners of Shaanxi recommended Zi as fit to command troops — obtained palace gate usher, made Zhenrong Army western-route overall inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Fan and Han recommended him; he became Zhenrong western inspector.

sentences.zh: 時京西軍賊張海久未伏誅，命滋都大提舉陝西、京西路捉賊，數月賊平。

translations.literal: At the time capital-west army bandit Zhang Hai long had not been executed — ordered Zi overall chief to arrest bandits in Shaanxi and western capital circuits — within several months bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He crushed Zhang Hai's bandit army within months as overall bandit hunter.

sentences.zh: 後為京東東路都巡檢。

translations.literal: Later became eastern-route overall inspector of the capital east.
translations.idiomatic: He then became eastern capital east-route inspector.

sentences.zh: 富弼為安撫使，舉再任登州。

translations.literal: Fu Bi as pacification commissioner recommended him for a second term at Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi recommended him for a second term at Deng.

sentences.zh: 乳山砦兵叛，殺巡檢，州將誅首惡數人，不窮按。

translations.literal: Rushan Stockade troops rebelled, killed the inspector — the prefecture general executed several chief villains, did not pursue fully.
translations.idiomatic: When Rushan garrison mutinied the prefect executed only a few ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 滋承檄驗治，馳入其壘，次第推問，得黨與百餘人付獄，眾莫敢動。

translations.literal: Zi received orders to verify and investigate, galloped into their camp, questioned in sequence, obtained accomplices more than a hundred handed to prison — the crowd did not dare stir.
translations.idiomatic: Zi rode into the camp, tried every man, and jailed a hundred accomplices.

sentences.zh: 在京東五年，數獲盜，不自言，弼為言，乃自東頭供奉官超授供備庫副使、定州路駐泊都監。

translations.literal: In the capital east five years, several times captured bandits without speaking himself — Bi spoke for him — thereupon from eastern-head palace attendant leap-appointed deputy commissioner of the supply depot and Dingzhou circuit garrison chief supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: After five years catching bandits quietly, Fu Bi secured his leap promotion to supply deputy and Dingzhou garrison chief.

sentences.zh: 嘗因給軍食，同列言粟不善，滋叱之曰：「爾欲以是怒眾耶？

translations.literal: Once because of issuing army grain, a colleague said the grain was not good — Zi rebuked him saying: "Do you wish to anger the masses with this?
translations.idiomatic: When a colleague called the rations bad Zi snapped, "Do you want to incite a mutiny?

sentences.zh: 使眾有一言，當先斬爾以徇。」

translations.literal: If the masses have one word, I should first behead you to display."
translations.idiomatic: If the men complain I will behead you first."

sentences.zh: 韓琦聞而壯之，以為真將帥材。

translations.literal: Han Qi heard and admired him, held him true general material.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi praised him as true general material.

sentences.zh: 及琦在河東，又奏滋權幷代路鈐轄，改管勾河東經略司公事。

translations.literal: When Qi was in Hedong, again memorialized Zi acting Bingdai circuit military inspector, changed to supervisor of Hedong frontier commission affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Hedong Han Qi made him acting Bingdai inspector and frontier commission supervisor.

sentences.zh: 建言：「代州、寧化軍有地萬頃，皆肥美，可募人田作，教戰射，為堡砦。」

translations.literal: He submitted saying: "Dai Prefecture and Ninghua Army have land ten thousand qing — all fertile and beautiful — can recruit people to farm fields, teach battle archery, make stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed farming ten thousand qing at Dai and Ninghua and training militia in fortified farms.

sentences.zh: 人以為利。

translations.literal: Men held it advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was welcomed.

sentences.zh: 累遷西上閤門副使，歷知安肅軍、保州。

translations.literal: Promoted in succession to deputy chief of the Western Upper Palace Gate, passed through prefect of Ansu Army and Bao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to deputy western palace gate chief and served as Ansu and Bao prefect.

sentences.zh: 滋強力精悍，有吏能，所至稱治。

translations.literal: Zi was strong, refined, and valiant, had clerk ability — wherever he went was called well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Strong and capable, he governed wherever he was posted.

sentences.zh: 會契丹民數違約，乘小舟漁界河中，吏憚生事，累歲莫敢禁。

translations.literal: It happened Khitan people several times violated treaty, riding small boats to fish in the border river — clerks feared creating incidents, years on none dared forbid.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan boats fished the border river for years while officials feared to stop them.

sentences.zh: 後又遣大舟十餘，自海口運鹽入界河。

translations.literal: Later again sent large boats more than ten, from the sea mouth transported salt into the border river.
translations.idiomatic: They then sent a dozen large boats hauling salt up the border river.

sentences.zh: 朝廷患之，以滋可任，徙知雄州。

translations.literal: The court worried — because Zi could be entrusted, shifted to prefect of Xiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Zi to Xiong to stop the incursions.

sentences.zh: 滋戒巡兵，舟至，輒捕其人殺之，輦其舟，移文還涿州，漁者遂絕。

translations.literal: Zi warned patrol troops — when boats arrived, always seized the men and killed them, carted off their boats, sent documents back to Zhuo Prefecture — fishermen then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Zi seized Khitan boats and crews and sent the boats back to Zhuo until fishing stopped.

sentences.zh: 契丹因使人以為言，而知瀛州彭思永、河北轉運使唐介燕度，皆以滋生事，請罷之。

translations.literal: The Khitan thereupon sent men to speak of it — yet Ying Prefecture's Peng Siyong and Hebei transport commissioner Tang Jie and Yan Du all because Zi created incidents, asked to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan protested and Peng Siyong and the transport commissioners tried to remove him for provoking trouble.

sentences.zh: 朝廷更以為能，擢龍神衛四廂都指揮使、嘉州團練使，遷天武、捧日四廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: The court on the contrary held him able — promoted overall commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard and regimental commander of Jia Prefecture, shifted to Tianwu and Penglai four wings overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Instead the court promoted him to dragon spirit and Tianwu-Penglai guard commander.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，領端州防禦使、步軍都虞候，賜白金五百兩，留再任。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, he held concurrently defender of Duan Prefecture and chief commandant of foot guards — granted five hundred taels white gold, retained for another term.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong made him foot-guard chief commandant with five hundred taels silver and kept him on.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，贈遂州觀察使。

translations.literal: Before long he died — posthumously made observation commissioner of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died and was posthumously made Suizhou observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 滋在雄州六年，契丹憚之。

translations.literal: Zi at Xiong Prefecture six years — the Khitan feared him.
translations.idiomatic: For six years at Xiong the Khitan feared him.

sentences.zh: 契丹嘗大饑，舊，米出塞不得過三斗，滋曰：「彼亦吾民也。」

translations.literal: The Khitan once suffered great famine — by old rule, rice leaving the pass could not exceed three dou — Zi said: "They are also Our people."
translations.idiomatic: During a Khitan famine Zi said, "They are our people too," and lifted the rice limit.

sentences.zh: 令出米無所禁，邊人德之。

translations.literal: He ordered rice issued without any prohibition — border people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: He let grain flow freely and the border people blessed him.

sentences.zh: 馭軍嚴，戰卒舊不服役，滋役之如廂兵，莫敢有言。

translations.literal: He governed troops strictly — battle soldiers formerly did not perform corvée; Zi corvée'd them like wing troops, none dared have words.
translations.idiomatic: He made combat troops do corvée like garrison soldiers and none dared complain.

sentences.zh: 繕治城壁、樓櫓，至於簿書、米鹽，皆有條法。

translations.literal: He repaired city walls and tower watchtowers — reaching to ledgers, rice and salt, all had regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt walls and towers and regulated every ledger down to salt rations.

sentences.zh: 性尤廉謹，月得公使酒，不以入家。

translations.literal: His nature especially honest and careful — monthly public envoy wine obtained, he did not bring into the household.
translations.idiomatic: So honest he never took official wine home.

sentences.zh: 然傲慢自譽，此其短也。

translations.literal: Yet arrogant self-praise — this was his shortcoming.
translations.idiomatic: His flaw was arrogance and self-praise.

sentences.zh: 論曰：石普曉暢軍事，習知民庸，然揣麾時政，終以罪廢。

translations.literal: The commentators say: Shi Pu understood military affairs clearly and was versed in civilian labor — yet he gauged and waved at court politics and in the end was dismissed for crime.
translations.idiomatic: The historians say Shi Pu knew war and labor yet meddled in politics and ended disgraced.

sentences.zh: 張孜雖稱持重，跡其所長，無足取者。

translations.literal: Zhang Zi though called steady and weighty — tracing what he excelled at, there was nothing worth taking.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zi, called steady, had little to his credit.

sentences.zh: 許懷德以懦不任事，數遭貶斥，其不及普遠矣。

translations.literal: Xu Huaide because cowardly did not bear affairs, several times met demotion and rejection — he fell far short of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Cowardly Xu Huaide, repeatedly demoted, was no match for Pu.

sentences.zh: 劉文質以私錢給軍，且脫人於死，仕雖偃蹇，聲名俱章章矣。

translations.literal: Liu Wenzhi with private money supplied the army and moreover released men from death — office though stumbling, fame and reputation both were illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenzhi, who paid armies from his purse and spared lives, kept a shining name despite setbacks.

sentences.zh: 渙以小官，能抗疏母后，輯暴弭奸，則其餘事也。

translations.literal: Huan with a small office could resist memorial to the empress dowager, gather violence and stop treachery — then the rest were minor matters.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's defiance of the empress dowager and suppression of villains overshadowed his other deeds.

sentences.zh: 滬，水洛之戰，從容退師，滬之才略，其最優者歟？

translations.literal: Hu — at Shuiluo battle, calmly withdrew the army — Hu's talent and stratagem, was it not the finest?
translations.idiomatic: Was Hu's calm withdrawal at Shuiluo not his finest hour?

sentences.zh: 趙滋有吏能，出米塞下以振契丹，亦仁人之用心。

translations.literal: Zhao Zi had clerk ability, issued rice below the pass to relieve the Khitan — also a benevolent man's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zi's grain to starving Khitan showed a humane heart.

sentences.zh: 李允則在河北二十年，設施方略，不動聲氣，契丹至以長者稱之。

translations.literal: Li Yunze in Hebei twenty years, deploying stratagems without moving sound or breath — the Khitan even called him a man of long standing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yunze ruled Hebei twenty years so quietly the Khitan called him a elder statesman.

sentences.zh: 張亢起儒生，曉韜略，琉璃堡、兔毛川之捷，良快人意，區區書生，功名如此，何其壯哉！

translations.literal: Zhang Kang rose from Confucian student, understood military stratagems — Liuli Stockade and Tumao River victories truly pleased men's hearts; a mere bookish student, achievement and fame thus — how bold!
translations.idiomatic: Scholar Zhang Kang's victories at Liuli and Tumaomao were thrilling proof that a literatus could win glory.

sentences.zh: 奎以治跡著稱，其視亢蓋所謂難為兄難為弟者歟？

translations.literal: Kui with traces of good governance was renowned — his view of Kang is perhaps what is called hard to be elder brother, hard to be younger brother?
translations.idiomatic: Kui's governance fame makes the brothers a pair hard to rank—who was the greater?
